Verified safe — ios/EatPal/EatPal/Services/EdgeFunctions.swift sets 'Authorization: Bearer <session access token>' on every invoke (falling back to the anon key only when there is genuinely no session), and Android goes through supabase.client.functions.invoke, which attaches the session token via the SDK. The pattern is already shipped and proven: parse-recipe (the share-extension path) and tonight-mode are both requireUser-gated today. userStories.title: Authorize process-delivery-order against the caller's household
userStories.description: As a parent, I want only my household to see and change my grocery delivery orders, so that a stranger cannot cancel my delivery or read my address.
acceptanceCriteria: process-delivery-order is gated with requireUser and returns 401 for an anonymous caller
userId is derived from the verified token, not read from the request body
householdId from the body is verified against household_members before any read or write, mirroring the pattern already used by tonight-mode
All five actions (estimate, create, submit, status, cancel) are covered by the check — not just the mutating ones
Tests cover: anonymous rejected, authenticated caller cannot act on a household they do not belong to, and a member can act on their own
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED + VERIFIED 2026-08-08. process-delivery-order now gates on requireUser before anything else, and derives identity from the verified token rather than the body: request.userId is overwritten with gate.userId, so a caller can no longer create an order attributed to someone else. Added two authorization helpers mirroring tonight-mode's approach — memberOfHousehold() checks household_members, and canAccessOrder() loads the grocery_delivery_orders row and accepts it only when order.user_id matches the caller or the caller belongs to order.household_id. Both checks run for ALL FIVE actions rather than only the mutating ones, because estimate and status leak another household's basket and delivery address just as readily as cancel destroys their order. A service-role caller (gate.role === 'service') is exempt and keeps the body-supplied ids, since scheduled function-to-function invokes have no user identity of their own and already hold a trusted key. New code avoids `any` via a SupabaseLike alias; the pre-existing `any` handler signatures were left alone rather than widening the diff.

userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED + VERIFIED 2026-08-08. Root cause was one missing polyfill: jsdom has no ResizeObserver, @radix-ui/react-use-size constructs one on mount, InputOTP pulls it in, so the Auth page threw during layout effects and rendered an EMPTY tree. Added a ResizeObserver stub to src/test/setup.ts (matchMedia and IntersectionObserver were already mocked there, so only this one was missing). Then tightened the assertions, which is the part that actually matters: the old tests asserted `length).toBeGreaterThan(0)` against an empty tree, so they compared 0 to 0 — they caught the breakage only by accident and would have PASSED a blank page had the comparison gone the other way. Also fixed three mocks that named functions the real modules do not export — trackConversion/trackSignUp/trackLogin instead of trackSignup/trackPageView, recordLoginAttempt/Success/Failure instead of logLogin/logFailedLogin, and remainingAttempts instead of remaining — every one of which would have thrown the moment a test exercised a submit path, which is precisely why none did. Added sign-in coverage per the AC: limiter rejection makes NO credential call, a failure records the attempt and logs it, and success clears both limiters and calls loginHistory.logLogin (also asserting the US-617 clear_login_rate_limit RPC). VERIFIED NOT VACUOUS: removing the polyfill again fails 8 of 9 (only the trivial document.body smoke check survives). Full suite now 1362 passed, 0 failed — the ci.yml:90 vitest gate is green again.

userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-08, WITH A MATERIAL CORRECTION TO THE STORY. The original ACs said to delete the top-level functions/ tree as dead. That would have been DESTRUCTIVE: it holds the entire Agentic OS (33 directories that exist nowhere else — agent-*, dispatcher, approval-executor, support-intake, csat-rate, nurture-unsubscribe, health-check) plus ~75 shared logic modules with their Deno tests, and ci.yml:182,187 runs `deno test functions/_shared/...` on every push. It is not dead and was not deleted. The real structure, which nothing in the repo previously recorded: the two trees target DIFFERENT RUNTIMES. All 93 handlers in supabase/functions/ use `export default async (req)`, which is exactly what edge-functions-server.ts calls via module.default(req), and both Dockerfiles copy that tree — so it is what serves production. The 48 in functions/ use serve() (Deno std / Supabase CLI style). That is the precise mechanism behind US-616: the Stripe idempotency guard was written in the serve() tree, which the live server cannot load at all, so it never deployed. Delivered: scripts/ci/check-function-trees.sh, wired into the quality job as a hard gate, failing on (1) a FUNCTIONS_MAP entry with no directory in the deployed tree and (2) any NEW cross-tree name collision, with the 15 existing collisions listed explicitly following the same grandfathering convention as check-migration-prefixes.sh. Verified not vacuous: injecting a fake collision and a fake unroutable map entry each fail the gate; the clean tree passes. Plus docs/EDGE_FUNCTION_TREES.md documenting the split, the trap, the guard, and where to add a new function. Reconciling the 15 existing collisions is deliberately NOT done here — one of them (create-checkout) is the payments entry point with a genuinely newer non-deployed copy, split out as US-626. || ROUND 19 2026-08-23 (loop) - THE GATE'S OWN THIRD CHECK CAUGHT A PAIR THIS STORY'S NOTES SAID WAS CLEAN, AND THE EARLIER VERIFICATION WAS THE THING THAT WAS WRONG. Merging #248 turned ci.yml red on main at 'Check edge-function trees': functions/tonight-mode (2026-06-13, a3e97d5e) is newer than supabase/functions/tonight-mode (2026-06-02, 013e0efe). These notes claim the opposite for tonight-mode, re-verified 2026-08-19. WHY BOTH THAT CHECK AND MINE MISSED IT: a shallow clone makes `git log -1 --format=%ct -- <path>` return the boundary commit for BOTH paths, so the timestamps compare equal and check 3/3 cannot fail. This file already documents that degradation ('a shallow clone degrades to the old behaviour'); what it did not anticipate is someone verifying the claim IN one. Every 'check-function-trees OK' run in this container was vacuous for check 3 until `git fetch --unshallow` (319 commits -> 1827). NOT A PRODUCTION HOLE, checked rather than assumed: a3e97d5e was the US-324 batch, which added assertHouseholdMember to the LEGACY copy and never touched the deployed one - but the deployed copy already enforces the same rule inline, querying household_members before trusting a body-supplied householdId (supabase/functions/tonight-mode/index.ts:185-195), which is where US-312 put it. The two files are not variants of one implementation; deployed is the newer US-312 rewrite and legacy is the older US-293 design plus a scoring.ts. So there is nothing to port. RESOLVED THE WAY THIS STORY RESOLVED create-checkout: deleted functions/tonight-mode/ and removed it from KNOWN_COLLISIONS (14 -> 13, header counts updated). functions/_shared/household.ts is now consumer-less and is KEPT, because functions/_shared/helpers_test.ts covers isHouseholdMember/assertHouseholdMember and ci.yml runs those Deno tests - the same disposition stripe-prices.ts got. Its header now says so. VERIFIED WITH FULL HISTORY, which is the only run that means anything here: gate exit 0, and the negative control still fails - committing an edit to functions/stripe-webhook makes check 3 name that pair and exit 1. 1720 tests pass. userStories.title: Stop the functions server leaking stack traces and enumerating its own routes
userStories.description: As a security-conscious operator, I want error responses and health checks to reveal nothing useful to an attacker, so that probing the functions host does not hand over a map of the surface.
acceptanceCriteria: The 500 handler logs the stack server-side and returns only a generic message plus a correlation id — no message/stack in the response body
GET /health returns liveness only; it no longer lists every available function name
The response-header merge stops overwriting each function's own Access-Control-Allow-Origin with '*', so the allowlists computed by common/headers.ts and _shared/cors.ts actually take effect
The per-request Deno.env.set() calls are removed; env is read once at module scope
If US-622 concludes this file is dead, deleting it satisfies this story — record that decision in the notes rather than leaving both paths live
userStories.notes: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-08. Correction to the story's last AC: edge-functions-server.ts is NOT dead, so the 'deleting it satisfies this story' escape hatch does not apply — it is the LIVE runtime. Evidence: all 93 deployed handlers export a bare default function, which is the contract this server calls (module.default(req)) and not the Deno.serve shape the Supabase CLI expects; the root Dockerfile runs `deno run server.ts` against it. Fixed in place: (1) the 500 handler no longer returns message/stack — it logs them server-side against a crypto.randomUUID() correlation id and returns only that id, so an operator can still tie a report to a trace; (2) /health returns liveness only, no longer enumerating the whole FUNCTIONS_MAP to any unauthenticated caller, and the 404 branch no longer echoes the routing table either; (3) the CORS merge now fills in only headers the function did NOT set, instead of unconditionally overwriting — the previous behaviour replaced the per-function origin allowlist computed by common/headers.ts and _shared/cors.ts with '*' on every single response, silently defeating it; (4) the per-request Deno.env.set() calls are gone (they wrote process-global state on every request to re-set values already read from the same environment at startup), replaced by a boot-time readiness check that logs loudly when SUPABASE_URL / ANON_KEY / SERVICE_ROLE_KEY are missing. NOTE: the server still answers OPTIONS preflight itself with '*' before routing; the actual response now carries the function's own origin header, so the allowlist is effective on the response that matters, but routing preflight to the function would be a cleaner follow-up.

userStories.title: Audit the diverged create-checkout implementations
userStories.description: As a customer starting a subscription, I want the deployed checkout handler to be the current one, so that fixes written since June are actually live.
acceptanceCriteria: Diff functions/create-checkout/index.ts (2026-07-11) against supabase/functions/create-checkout/index.ts (2026-06-13) and enumerate every behavioural difference, not just the runtime shape
Decide which behaviours are correct; port anything missing into supabase/functions/create-checkout (the deployed tree)
Pay particular attention to price resolution: the top-level copy imports resolvePriceId from _shared/stripe-prices.ts while the deployed copy does not
Confirm the deployed handler validates the caller and the requested plan before creating a Stripe session
Delete the non-deployed copy once reconciled, and remove it from KNOWN_COLLISIONS in scripts/ci/check-function-trees.sh
userStories.notes: Resolved 2026-08-19. DIFF: the two copies were not variants but different contracts. Deployed (supabase/functions) takes {planId, billingCycle, successUrl, cancelUrl} and returns {url}; top-level took {price_id|plan} and returned {checkout_url}. src/pages/Pricing.tsx:233 is the ONLY caller in the repo (no iOS/Android caller - grepped ios/, android-native/, app/) and it sends the deployed shape and reads data.url, so the top-level copy had never been callable: deploying it would have broken checkout. PRICE RESOLUTION: the resolvePriceId concern does not apply - the deployed handler never accepts a price from the caller. It takes a planId, reads the price columns off the subscription_plans row server-side, and then verifies the price exists in Stripe. That is a stronger guard against US-326 price/tier tampering than the env allowlist, which still trusts a client-supplied price_id and only checks membership. CALLER/PLAN VALIDATION CONFIRMED: JWT verified via supabase.auth.getUser(token) before anything else, and the plan is fetched by id (404 if absent) before the Stripe session. PORTED into the deployed tree: non-POST -> 405; missing STRIPE_SECRET_KEY -> 503 instead of an opaque Stripe failure; real status codes (401 auth, 400 bad request, 404 plan, 502 customer, 500 unexpected) in place of a blanket 400; body-shape validation (planId string, billingCycle monthly|yearly); client_reference_id on the session; and the US-532 fix - the old code returned error.message verbatim, which src/lib/edge-functions.ts hands straight to the browser, leaking Stripe price IDs, customer IDs and upstream Stripe text. All errors now go through one fail() that logs the detail server-side and returns a coarse message plus a stable code. Messages deliberately keep the words 'Price' and 'Customer' because Pricing.tsx:250-256 string-matches on them to pick its toast. KEPT from the deployed copy: trial wiring (US-630), customer reuse/recreate, price existence check, securityHeaders. Also dropped the three `any` catch annotations for a typed errMessage() helper. DELETED functions/create-checkout/ and removed create-checkout from KNOWN_COLLISIONS in scripts/ci/check-function-trees.sh (15 -> 14, header counts updated); the gate exits 0. functions/_shared/stripe-prices.ts is now consumer-less - kept with its Deno tests (functions/_shared/helpers_test.ts, run by ci.yml:181) and its header rewritten to say so. VERIFIED: check-function-trees.sh exit 0; src/lib/trialDisclosure.test.ts 20/20 (its 4 structural guards read the rewritten file); eslint clean on the changed file. NOTE for follow-up: a THIRD copy exists at coolify-migration/eatpal-functions-package/create-checkout/index.ts, a 2026-06-27 snapshot that is now behind by the US-630 trial block and this change. It is not built by either Dockerfile or edge-functions-server.ts and is outside this story's ACs, but it is a stale artifact someone could mistake for live code. || RE-VERIFIED + GATE HARDENED 2026-08-19 (loop). Re-checked the claim that the other 13 collisions are benign, since several 'blocked' premises in this prd have gone stale. It HOLDS: for every one of ai-meal-plan, calculate-food-similarity, generate-blog-content, generate-sitemap, generate-social-content, identify-product, parse-receipt-image, parse-recipe, stripe-webhook, suggest-foods, suggest-recipe, tonight-mode and update-blog-image, the DEPLOYED copy's last commit is newer than or the same date as the top-level one. No unshipped work is hiding in the non-deployed tree. BUT THE GATE COULD NOT HAVE TOLD US THAT. check-function-trees.sh only blocked NEW collisions; it had no way to see an EXISTING pair drifting, which is the exact shape of the US-616 incident its own header describes — the Stripe idempotency work landed in the serve() tree the live server cannot load, never shipped, and the dedup table stayed empty for a month. Added a third check: for each known collision, compare last-commit timestamps and fail when the non-deployed copy is newer. Verified by simulating exactly that (an edit to functions/stripe-webhook/index.ts) — the gate fails naming the pair and telling you to port or delete. Skips a pair rather than failing when either timestamp is unavailable, so a shallow clone degrades to the old behaviour; CI uses fetch-depth: 0 (ci.yml:26) so it has the history it needs. This means the next US-616 is caught by CI on the commit that causes it rather than by someone noticing a month later.

userStories.title: Stop anonymous enumeration of the profile-pictures bucket
userStories.description: As a parent, I want my child's photo to be reachable only by me, so that an anonymous client cannot list the bucket and pull down every child's face stored in EatPal.
acceptanceCriteria: New migration replaces the SELECT policy "Users can view all profile pictures" on storage.objects (created in 20251008025307_8faf3224-9a40-415e-9176-ccaa98641861.sql:6-8) with one scoped to the owning user - (storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text - plus the existing admin role check

Before writing the migration, confirm no shipped iOS build calls list() or select on storage.objects for this bucket: grep ios/EatPal for storage list/download calls. Reads of an existing public URL bypass RLS, so they are unaffected; a client that LISTS would break

Bucket stays public = true in this story so URLs already stored in kids.profile_picture_url keep rendering on shipped iOS builds. Full private + signed URLs is US-634 and is gated on a force-update mechanism that does not exist yet

New uploads use an unguessable object name: replace `${user.id}/${Date.now()}.${ext}` with `${user.id}/${crypto.randomUUID()}.${ext}` in ManageKidsDialog.tsx:186 and OnboardingDialog.tsx:135, and in the iOS uploader if it builds its own path
supabase/functions/update-blog-image/index.ts:60,73 stops writing blog images into profile-pictures; point it at the generated-images bucket instead
Test proves an anon-key client cannot list objects in profile-pictures and an authenticated client can only list its own folder
Migration is additive/policy-only (no DROP COLUMN, DROP TABLE, or RENAME); npm run typecheck and npm run test:run pass
userStories.notes:
Shipped 2026-08-17. Migration 20260817000000_scope_profile_picture_reads.sql drops the unrestricted "Users can view all profile pictures" SELECT policy (which applied to the public role, so anon could list the whole bucket) and replaces it with an authenticated, owner-scoped policy matching on (storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text OR owner = auth.uid(), plus an admin policy via the user_roles pattern so StorageManagement.tsx keeps working. Bucket deliberately STAYS public = true: shipped iOS renders kids.profile_picture_url as a plain public URL (Kid.swift:11) and there is no force-update gate, so a private flip would break every phone in the field. Public URL reads bypass RLS and are unaffected; only enumeration is closed. US-634 finishes the job. Upload paths now use generateId() from src/lib/utils instead of Date.now() (ManageKidsDialog.tsx:189, OnboardingDialog.tsx:137) so a path is unguessable while the bucket is still URL-readable. update-blog-image now writes to generated-images instead of storing blog artwork beside photographs of children; existing blog URLs still resolve because the old bucket stays public. New guard src/lib/storageBucketPolicies.test.ts scans every migration for a net-live unrestricted SELECT on storage.objects (tracking DROP POLICY so history does not false-positive, allowlisting generated-images as intentionally world-readable) and asserts both upload sites avoid timestamp paths; mutation-checked by removing the DROP and confirming it fails. Verified before writing: no shipped iOS build lists this bucket - ImageUploadService targets a DIFFERENT bucket and only calls upload/getPublicURL/remove.
OPEN: (1) the live-database assertion (anon list returns nothing, authenticated list returns only own folder) is not covered - the repo has no RLS integration harness, so the guard is static-only. (2) iOS uploads kid photos to an undeclared 'images' bucket that is not in any migration and could carry the same hole - filed as US-635, and this story does NOT close that exposure. (3) npm run lint is red repo-wide on clean HEAD (1507 problems, 1239 errors); verified identical before and after these changes, so no regression, but the gate is unusable as a signal.

userStories.title: Delete stored images when a kid profile or account is deleted
userStories.description: As a parent who deletes my account, I want the photos I uploaded to actually be gone, so that the deletion promised in the Privacy Policy is the deletion that happens.
acceptanceCriteria: supabase/functions/delete-account/index.ts lists everything under `${userId}/` in profile-pictures and removes it before calling auth.admin.deleteUser (currently lines 90-113 delete DB rows only and never touch storage)
Storage removal failures land in the same `failures` map as table failures so a partial delete is visible rather than silent
Deleting a kid removes that kid's photo object: derive the storage path from kids.profile_picture_url in the deleteKid path used by ManageKidsDialog.tsx:231
Replacing a kid's photo removes the previous object instead of orphaning it (both upload sites: ManageKidsDialog.tsx:189, OnboardingDialog.tsx:139)
Deletion is best-effort and never blocks the account delete from completing
Tests cover: account delete removes the user's storage folder; kid delete removes only that kid's object; photo replace removes the old object
npm run typecheck and npm run test:run pass
userStories.notes:
Shipped 2026-08-18. New src/lib/storagePaths.ts parses a stored public or signed URL back into {bucket, path} (refusing traversal), and src/lib/storageCleanup.ts wraps it in deleteStorageObject / deleteReplacedStorageObject - always best-effort, logged, never thrown, so a Storage failure can never block a user's delete.
delete-account now reads kids.profile_picture_url BEFORE the table scrub, parses each URL, and removes those objects plus everything under {userId}/ in profile-pictures, all before auth.admin.deleteUser. Reading the URLs first is what makes this cover iOS photos too: they land in the 'images' bucket at kids/{kidId}-{unix}.jpg with no user prefix, so a folder sweep alone would miss every one of them. Storage failures record into the existing `failures` map as storage:<bucket> rather than aborting.
KidsContext.deleteKid captures the photo URL before the optimistic delete and removes the object only after the server delete succeeds, so a rolled-back delete cannot destroy the photo of a child that came back. Both upload dialogs now delete the object they replace (ManageKidsDialog.tsx:204, OnboardingDialog.tsx:151), which previously orphaned every superseded photo in a URL-readable bucket.
Tests: storagePaths.test.ts (12) covers both bucket layouts, query strings, signed URLs, percent-encoding, non-storage URLs and traversal; storageCleanup.test.ts (13) covers removal, the no-op cases, error and throw paths, replace-vs-unchanged, and four structural guards on the Deno handler (photo lookup precedes the scrub, removal precedes the auth delete, the folder sweep exists, no throw in the storage block).
OPEN: (1) the Deno handler is guarded structurally, not behaviourally - end-to-end coverage (upload, delete account, confirm the object is gone) needs the same integration harness US-627 wants. (2) The parser is duplicated between src/lib/storagePaths.ts and the Deno function because the two trees cannot share code; the copy is commented as a mirror. (3) Photos uploaded by iOS before a kid row was deleted on an older client are already orphaned in the images bucket - a one-off reconciliation sweep is not part of this story.

userStories.title: Crisis and scope guardrails in the AI coach
userStories.description: As a parent describing a frightening feeding situation, I want the AI coach to point me at real help instead of coaching me through it, so that a nutrition chatbot is not the thing standing between a child and care.

Audit the other free-text AI surfaces (tonight-mode, suggest-foods, ai-meal-plan) and note which need the same block; implement where the user can type prose
npm run typecheck and npm run test:run pass
userStories.notes:
Shipped 2026-08-18. New supabase/functions/_shared/safety.ts holds the model-facing rules in two blocks. CRISIS_PROMPT_BLOCK covers self-harm/suicidal statements, eating-disorder signals (restriction, fear of eating, purging, hiding food, weight distress, refusal causing weight loss) and medical symptoms (choking, trouble swallowing, allergic reaction, dehydration, failure to gain weight), and tells the model to STOP coaching, acknowledge briefly, name ONE matching resource, and not diagnose or counsel. STANDING_LIMITS_BLOCK forbids diagnosis, medical/medication advice, calorie targets or weight-management plans for a child, and pressure/bribe/punish/withhold feeding tactics.
Split deliberately: the crisis half only matters where a user can type prose, so withSafetyRules() (both blocks) goes on ai-coach-chat, and withStandingLimits() (limits only) goes on ai-meal-plan, suggest-recipe and suggest-foods - a meal plan carrying a calorie target is the same problem as a chat message carrying one, but paying crisis-block tokens on every structured generation is not.
Audit result for the other AI surfaces: only ai-coach-chat accepts free-text prose. tonight-mode (householdId/kidIds/numbers), ai-meal-plan (kid fields + food lists), suggest-foods and suggest-recipe all take structured input, and ai-meal-plan does not read kids.notes, so no free-text crisis channel reaches them.
Resources live in SAFETY_RESOURCES, mirrored to src/lib/aiSafety.ts for UI copy because the Deno and web trees cannot share modules. src/lib/aiSafety.test.ts (13 tests) fails if the two lists drift, if the crisis/limits language is weakened, or if any of the four functions stops wrapping its prompt. AIMealCoach.tsx now renders AI_COACH_DISCLAIMER plus CRISIS_HELP_LINE under the composer, so 988 and the ANAD number are on screen rather than depending on the model to produce them.
OPEN: (1) the guardrail is asserted structurally - there is no eval harness proving the model actually complies, which is the only way to know it works; worth building before this is relied on. (2) Resources are US-only; an international user gets a US number. (3) The disclaimer renders with an open conversation, not on the empty state. (4) Per the compliance-audit convention, user-facing safety copy still wants counsel review before ship.

userStories.title: Make the advertised free trial real, or stop advertising it
userStories.description: As someone clicking 'Start Free Trial', I want either a trial or honest pricing copy, so that I am not charged immediately by a button that promised otherwise.
acceptanceCriteria: First establish ground truth: check whether trial_period_days is configured on the Stripe Prices themselves, since supabase/functions/create-checkout/index.ts:132-155 sets neither trial_period_days nor subscription_data.trial_settings
If no trial exists and the product should have one: add trial_period_days to the checkout session, sourced from a new nullable column on subscription_plans (additive migration), not hardcoded
If no trial exists and the product should not have one: remove the claim from Landing.tsx:954, :978, :1030 and Pricing.tsx:506
If a trial ships, the CTA carries the ROSCA disclosure adjacent to the button: what is charged, when the first charge lands, and how to cancel
stripe-webhook already persists trial_end (index.ts:298) - confirm it populates for trialing subscriptions end to end
Reconcile every other surface that mentions a trial so one answer is true everywhere
npm run typecheck and npm run test:run pass
userStories.notes:
Shipped 2026-08-18. Product decision from Dj: EatPal should have a trial, so this was implemented rather than the copy removed.
Ground truth first: nothing in the repo configured a trial anywhere - no column on subscription_plans, no trial_period_days or trial_settings in create-checkout, and the stripe-events/sub-events/checkout-events fixtures at the repo root are empty Stripe list responses (UTF-16 encoded), so they carry no evidence either way. Whether the live Stripe Prices carry a trial is still unverified from here; if they do, the price-level trial and this session-level one both apply and the session value wins, so confirm in the dashboard.
Migration 20260818000000_add_plan_trial_period.sql adds a NULLABLE trial_period_days to subscription_plans (additive; shipped iOS selects * and ignores unknown keys) and seeds 7 for every plan with price_monthly > 0. Length is data so it changes without a deploy, and a plan opts out by leaving it NULL. create-checkout reads plan.trial_period_days and, only when it is a finite number > 0, passes subscription_data.trial_period_days plus trial_settings.end_behavior.missing_payment_method = 'cancel' - Checkout always collects a card in subscription mode, so a trial ending without one means the card was pulled or declined, and cancelling beats leaving a subscription the user still sees as active.
Disclosure: src/lib/trialDisclosure.ts builds the ROSCA sentence (amount, cadence, advance notice, how to cancel) from the same plan row checkout reads, so the page cannot promise something Stripe will not do. Rendered under both Pricing CTAs - the actual consent point, where a card is committed - and under both Landing plan CTAs. Pricing's summary line no longer says the bare 'Free trial available'.
Webhook verified end to end: handleSubscriptionUpdated persists status (including 'trialing') and trial_end at index.ts:294,298; the only trial_end: null writes are the cancellation and downgrade paths, which is correct. create-checkout upserts the row first, so the update branch is the one that runs.
Tests: trialDisclosure.test.ts (20) covers the copy, pluralisation, the no-trial null cases, first-charge date arithmetic and non-mutation, four structural guards on the Deno checkout handler (reads the plan row not a literal, reaches subscription_data, cancels on missing payment method, omits trial config when there is none), and a guard that any page saying 'free trial' also renders the disclosure.
OPEN: (1) Landing hardcodes its prices and now its trial length via MARKETING_TRIAL_DAYS; a test fails if that constant stops matching the seeded value, but the PRICES on Landing are still hardcoded and can drift from the database independently - pre-existing, not fixed here. (2) 7 days is my default, not a decision Dj made - change the seeded value if it should differ, and the drift test will point at the constant to update. (3) Confirm in the Stripe dashboard that the Prices do not also carry a trial.

userStories.title: Trial-ending reminder job, or remove the dead trial automation
userStories.description: As a trial user, I want warning before my card is charged, so that the conversion is something I chose rather than something that happened to me.
acceptanceCriteria: Blocked on US-630: if that story concludes there is no trial, this story is closed by deleting src/lib/trial-automation.ts and the trial_ending options in WorkflowBuilder.tsx:107 and EmailSequenceBuilder.tsx:100 rather than by building a job

If a trial exists: a scheduled edge function (pg_cron, matching the existing scheduled-function pattern) selects user_subscriptions where status = 'trialing' and trial_end falls in the 3-day and 1-day windows
Sends through the existing send-emails function using the trial_ending_3d and trial_ending_1d template keys that src/lib/trial-automation.ts:229,243 already names

Idempotent: a row in subscription_notifications with notification_type = 'trial_ending' (type already exists per 20251030000001_subscription_enhancements.sql:11) prevents a second send for the same window
The reminder states the charge amount, the charge date, and a one-click path to cancel
src/lib/trial-automation.ts is either wired into the live path or deleted - it is currently imported by nothing and reads as working code
npm run typecheck and npm run test:run pass
userStories.notes:
Shipped 2026-08-18. Not closed by deletion: US-630 concluded EatPal should have a trial, so the reminder was built.
New supabase/functions/schedule-trial-reminders runs daily, selects user_subscriptions where status = 'trialing' and trial_end falls inside the UTC day 3 days out and 1 day out, and queues into automation_email_queue, which the existing send-emails drainer delivers. Migration 20260818000001 seeds the trial_ending_3d and trial_ending_1d templates the dead library already named (the queue has an FK to automation_email_templates.template_key, so the insert would have failed without them).
Idempotency is a partial UNIQUE index over (user_id, metadata->>'stripe_subscription_id', metadata->>'window') WHERE notification_type = 'trial_ending'. The job writes the notification row FIRST and treats a 23505 as already-sent, so the database claims the send rather than the code checking-then-writing; an overlapping cron fire or a retry cannot double-send even if the email insert afterwards fails. Partial because no row currently uses that notification_type, so the index cannot conflict with existing data. Per-subscription failures are caught and counted, so one bad row cannot kill the run.
Each reminder states the plan, the exact trial-end date, the amount and cadence, and that cancelling before then means no charge, with a link to /dashboard/billing (two clicks to cancel, per the existing flow). Priority 8 rather than the default 5: missing this one costs the user money.
src/lib/trial-automation.ts (509 lines, four exported functions, imported by nothing) is deleted - it read as working code and was not.
Tests: src/lib/trialReminders.test.ts (11) guards the trialing filter, both windows, the claim-before-queue ordering, the 23505 skip, the money terms in the copy, per-row error isolation, the seeded templates, the uniqueness and partiality of the index, cancellation wording in both templates, and that the new templates do not carry the purple gradient the house style bans.
OPEN: (1) The cron job is NOT scheduled - the SQL is in the function's header comment, matching how schedule-weekly-reports documents itself, and someone has to run cron.schedule against production. Until that happens no reminder sends, so this is the one step that must not be skipped at deploy. (2) The amount always reads price_monthly; current_period length is not stored on user_subscriptions, so a yearly trial would quote a monthly figure. Correct fix is to record the billing cycle at checkout. (3) The trial_ending options in WorkflowBuilder.tsx:107 and EmailSequenceBuilder.tsx:100 are left in place - they belong to the separate configurable-workflow system, and whether that engine actually fires is out of scope here. (4) No integration test; needs a database and a Stripe fixture.

userStories.title: Disclose photo collection and label AI in-product
userStories.description: As a user pointing my camera at my fridge, I want to know the photo leaves EatPal for a third-party AI, so that I can decide before the shutter rather than after.
acceptanceCriteria: Privacy Policy section 2 lists the images actually collected: child profile photos, food photos, receipt photos, fridge photos
Privacy Policy section 6 states that photos submitted to AI features are transmitted to the LLM provider, are not stored by us server-side, and are not used to train models
One-line notice in the capture UI before submission - ImageFoodCapture.tsx, the receipt scanner, and the fridge scanner - saying the photo is sent to a third-party AI provider to identify items
AI coach responses carry an AI-generated label (pairs with the disclaimer in US-629)
Verify and keep the current server behaviour: identify-food-image, parse-receipt-image, and recognize-fridge-contents pass base64 straight through without persisting it - add a test if none pins this
New legal copy carries the same DRAFT / counsel-review marker as the rest of PrivacyPolicy.tsx
npm run typecheck and npm run test:run pass
userStories.notes:
Shipped 2026-08-18. Privacy Policy section 2 now lists the images actually collected (child profile photos; photos of food, grocery receipts and fridges submitted to recognition features), which were absent from the collection list entirely. Section 6 gains a 'Photos submitted to AI features' subsection explaining that the image is transmitted to the provider, passed through rather than stored, and that the business API terms do not use submitted content for training - deliberately phrased as what the providers' terms say rather than 'we do not permit', because the no-train/zero-retention request flag is still an open item from the July audit and I will not write a representation the code does not back. A second paragraph separates child profile photos, which ARE stored, are deleted with the profile or account (US-628), and never go to an AI provider. Last Updated moved to August 18, 2026.
In-product: PHOTO_AI_NOTICE in src/lib/aiSafety.ts renders in ImageFoodCapture and ScanReceiptDialog before submission, replacing dialogs whose only signal was 'Analyzing image...'. AI labelling on the coach is covered by the US-629 disclaimer plus the existing 'AI Meal Coach' heading and bot icon.
Verified and pinned: identify-food-image, parse-receipt-image and recognize-fridge-contents take base64 from the request body and hand it straight to the model. src/lib/photoPrivacy.test.ts (15) asserts none of the three writes to storage or inserts image data into a table, that the policy carries all three disclosures, and that both capture dialogs render the notice - so a later 'cache the uploads' change has to argue with a failing test.
OPEN: (1) recognize-fridge-contents has no web caller - it is reached from iOS, which has no equivalent notice; the iOS capture screen needs the same line. (2) Legal copy is DRAFT pending counsel, consistent with the rest of the July audit's additions. (3) The no-train/zero-retention provider flag is still not set on the requests themselves; the copy is written to stay true either way, but setting it would let the claim be stronger.

userStories.title: Open Food Facts attribution where its data is displayed
userStories.description: As the operator, I want to meet the ODbL attribution term, so that the product data we resell access to is licensed rather than borrowed.
acceptanceCriteria: Visible attribution wherever Open Food Facts sourced fields are rendered - barcode scan results and HarmonizedFoodDisplay.tsx - reading 'Data from Open Food Facts' and linking to openfoodfacts.org
Use src/lib/database-prioritization.ts to identify which displayed fields actually came from OFF rather than blanket-labelling every food
Attribution also appears in the Privacy Policy or a data-sources note alongside the USDA reference
Soften 'Official USDA data' on BudgetCalculator.tsx:299,517 to 'Based on USDA Food Plans data' so it reads as a source rather than an endorsement
npm run typecheck and npm run test:run pass
userStories.notes:
Shipped 2026-08-18. Correction to the story as written: the acceptance criteria pointed at src/lib/database-prioritization.ts and HarmonizedFoodDisplay.tsx, but both are dead scaffolding - referenced only by their own tests, and neither tracks a source at all. The live path is supabase/functions/lookup-barcode, which already tags every result with a source string ('Open Food Facts', 'USDA FoodData Central', 'FoodRepo', 'Your Pantry', 'Nutrition Database'), so attribution was wired to that instead.
New src/lib/dataSources.ts maps each source to its label, URL and licence, and src/components/DataSourceCredit.tsx renders the credit with links. It returns null for our own sources, which need none. Wired into BarcodeScannerDialog next to the record, because ODbL wants the credit where the data is shown rather than in a footer. FoodRepo is also ODbL and was credited at the same time.
Privacy Policy gains section 6a naming all three databases with links and licences, and stating plainly that they are sources we read from and none of them endorse EatPal.
USDA is public domain so it needed no licence notice, but 'Official USDA data' implied endorsement; reworded to 'Based on USDA Food Plans data' across BudgetCalculator.tsx, BudgetCalculatorResults.tsx, pdfGenerator.ts and en.json. The remaining 'official USDA' string is an internal code comment in usdaData.ts, which no user reads.

Also asserts every licensed source appears in the policy with its URL, that the scanner renders the credit, and that no user-facing file says 'official USDA'.
