(2) database-prioritization.ts and HarmonizedFoodDisplay.tsx are still present as dead code and are now doubly misleading, since they look like the data path and are not; worth deleting separately. (3) ODbL also has a share-alike term on derived databases - out of scope here, but relevant if EatPal ever redistributes a food dataset.

userStories.title: Move profile-pictures to a private bucket with signed URLs
userStories.description: As a parent, I want my child's photo behind an expiring signed URL, so that a leaked or shared link stops working instead of lasting forever.
acceptanceCriteria: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-19: this said no MIN_SUPPORTED_IOS_BUILD force-update gate exists. It does. US-380 shipped it under a different name, which is why a grep for the constant missed it: ios/EatPal/EatPal/Services/ForceUpdateService.swift reads min_ios_build from the app_config table, ForceUpdateView.swift is the screen, and RootView.swift:8,14 gates the whole app on it. It parses dotted CFBundleVersion (YYYYMMDD.run) rather than Int(), fails open on network error or unparseable config, and has Swift tests in ios/EatPal/EatPalTests/ForceUpdateServiceTests.swift

Prerequisite SATISFIED: the gate is shipped and seeded. supabase/migrations/20260614000000_app_config.sql creates app_config and seeds min_ios_build = 1, which blocks nobody until an admin bumps it. The remaining sequencing work below is therefore unblocked
Release N: clients request a signed URL through a helper instead of getPublicUrl; keep writing the public URL to kids.profile_picture_url so old clients keep working
Release N+1: once the min build is past N, migration sets profile-pictures public = false
Storage-object deletion from US-628 keeps working against the private bucket
Document the sequencing in the migration comment per the CLAUDE.md deprecation flow
userStories.notes: Found 2026-08-17. This is the correct end state for US-627, deliberately split out because it cannot ship backward-compatibly today. US-627 closes the enumeration hole and makes new paths unguessable while keeping shipped clients working; this story finishes the job once there is a version gate to hide behind. Do not start this before the force-update mechanism exists. || BLOCKER RE-VERIFIED AND FALSE 2026-08-19 (loop). The story was parked on 'no force-update gate exists'; US-380 built one and the story was never updated. Verified end to end: ForceUpdateService reads min_ios_build from app_config, RootView renders ForceUpdateView when needsUpdate, the app_config migration seeds min_ios_build = 1 so no existing install is blocked, and the build comparison is a tested value type that handles CI's dotted CFBundleVersion instead of collapsing it to 0. Both blocking ACs rewritten above rather than left to mislead the next reader. WHAT RELEASE N ACTUALLY NEEDS NOW, scoped from the code rather than guessed: five files read kid.profile_picture_url for rendering (ManageKidsDialog, FoodSuccessTracker, ApplyTemplateDialog and two others), all through . Release N means those read through a helper that mints a signed URL while upload KEEPS writing the plain public URL to kids.profile_picture_url, so shipped iOS builds — which render that column directly, Kid.swift:11 — keep working. src/lib/storage-manager.ts already has getSignedUrl and a signedUrlExpiry config, so the primitive exists; what does not exist is expiry handling at the render sites, and that is the real work: a signed URL expires, so an holding one goes broken on a long-lived tab unless the helper re-mints. NOT STARTED HERE deliberately — it changes how every kid avatar in the app renders and this container cannot verify it visually. US-627's read-scoping migration (20260817000000_scope_profile_picture_reads.sql) is already in place, so anonymous enumeration is closed; what is left is the public-by-URL exposure, which is what Release N+1 flipping public=false finally closes. || RELEASE N IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-19 (loop), now that the prerequisite turned out to be shipped. src/lib/profilePictureUrl.ts recovers the storage object path from a stored public URL and holds the refresh schedule; src/hooks/useSignedProfilePicture.ts mints a signed URL and re-mints 60s before the 600s expiry; src/components/KidAvatarImage.tsx is a drop-in for so each render site is a one-line swap and there is ONE place to change at Release N+1. Wired the three read-only sites (FoodSuccessTracker x2, ChildProfileCard, FamilyMealCard). DELIBERATELY NOT WIRED: ManageKidsDialog:288 and OnboardingDialog:321, which render formData.profile_picture_url — that value is a blob: preview of the file the user just picked, not a stored object, so signing it is meaningless; the helper returns null for blob:/data: URIs and falls through, but leaving those two on plain AvatarImage says so more clearly. THE DESIGN POINT: the hook returns the STORED PUBLIC URL until a signed one arrives, and permanently if signing fails. So this ships with zero visible change while the bucket is still public — which is the whole point of Release N, moving the web off public readability so Release N+1 can flip public=false without a flag day. Nothing changes what is WRITTEN: kids.profile_picture_url keeps holding a plain public URL, so shipped iOS builds rendering it directly (Kid.swift:11) keep working. 21 new tests: 16 on the pure path/schedule logic (including that a TTL shorter than the refresh margin cannot schedule in the past and re-mint on every render) and 5 on the hook (public URL rendered before any round trip, signed URL swapped in, public URL KEPT when signing fails rather than blanking an avatar, no signing attempted for a blob: preview). VERIFIED: full suite 1556 passed / 3 skipped, eslint clean on every changed file (the one remaining TrendingUp error in ChildProfileCard is pre-existing, confirmed by stashing), build exit 0 with 14/14 routes, new files ASCII. STILL OPEN: Release N+1 — the migration setting public=false, which must wait until app_config.min_ios_build is past the release that ships this, per the CLAUDE.md deprecation flow. || ROUND 2 2026-08-19 (loop) - RELEASE N WAS HALF-BLIND, AND THE RELEASE N+1 PLAN AS WRITTEN DOES NOT CLOSE THE STORY. Two findings, from reading the Swift client rather than the web one. (1) FIXED HERE: kids.profile_picture_url is written by TWO clients into TWO buckets. The web uploads to profile-pictures; iOS uploads kid photos to the 'images' bucket under kids/ (ImageUploadService.swift:8, bucketName = "images"). objectPathFromPublicUrl hardcoded 'profile-pictures', so every photo a parent uploaded from the phone was silently never signed - it fell through to the stored public URL, which looks identical while the bucket is public, and would have stayed publicly readable after Release N+1 closed the OTHER bucket. Now storageRefFromPublicUrl returns {bucket, path} and the hook signs against whatever the URL names. 6 new helper tests + 3 new hook tests; negative control run (pinning .from() back to 'profile-pictures' fails the iOS-upload test and nothing else). Full suite 1592 passed / 3 skipped, eslint clean. (2) NOT FIXED, NEEDS XCODE, AND IT BLOCKS RELEASE N+1: the iOS app has NO signed-URL path at all - grep for createSignedUrl across ios/ returns nothing. It renders kid.profilePictureUrl directly (one site: KidProfileEditorView.swift:70, via ImagePicker's currentURL:). A photo uploaded from the WEB lives in profile-pictures, so the moment Release N+1 flips that bucket to public=false, every iOS client rendering such a photo breaks - including builds already on phones. The plan in these notes ('bump min_ios_build past the release that ships this') does not cover it, because 'this' is the WEB signing work and bumping the min build does nothing for a Swift client that never learned to sign. iOS needs its own Release N (createSignedURL at that one render site, plus a decision about CachedAsyncImage, which keys its cache on the URL and would miss on every re-mint), and min_ios_build must be past THAT release, not this one. Sequenced correctly the flow is: Release N web (done) -> Release N iOS (needs Xcode) -> bump app_config.min_ios_build past the iOS release -> Release N+1 migration flips public=false on profile-pictures AND covers the images bucket (see US-635 query 4). || ROUND 3/4 2026-08-19 (loop) - RAN US-627's POLICY instead of trusting it. PostgreSQL 16 with a stand-in for Supabase's storage and auth schemas, the migration 20260817000000 applied verbatim. IT WORKS AS DOCUMENTED: before, anon enumerates all 4 seeded objects; after, anon 0, user A sees 2 (own folder plus a legacy object matched through the owner column - so that OR branch earns its place), user B sees 1 and none of A's, admin sees all 4. This is the first actual verification of the control that closed anonymous enumeration of a bucket full of photographs of children. NEW FINDING, and it is a US-634 pre-condition: an object with NO owner AND no user-id folder is visible to ADMINS ALONE - not to the parent whose child it is a photograph of. Harmless today (the bucket is public and the app falls back to the stored public URL) and BREAKING at Release N+1, because createSignedUrl requires the SELECT this policy denies, so a signed URL cannot be minted for such an object at all. Added query 5 to supabase/diagnostics/us-635-images-bucket.sql: profile-pictures objects split by whether they can be signed - via owner, via a first path segment that parses as a uuid, or neither. unsignable > 0 means US-634 needs an OWNER BACKFILL BEFORE the bucket is closed, not after. Verified against both awkward shapes (no owner + no folder, and no owner + a folder that is not a uuid). The proof is checked in as supabase/diagnostics/us-627-policy-check.sql - self-contained, runs against a throwaway database, expected output in its header. || ROUND 5 2026-08-19 (loop) - audited the migration-safety gate against the 207 migrations that already shipped, since backward compatibility is this story's whole sequencing problem. RESULT: zero migrations use DROP COLUMN, RENAME, SET NOT NULL or a type change, and the single DROP TABLE is the known scaffold cleanup - the repo has in fact followed CLAUDE.md's rule for the whole of its history, so the Release N+1 migration will be the unusual one and deserves the scrutiny. The gate's drop-policy rule was the outlier, firing on 30 of 207, because DROP POLICY IF EXISTS followed by CREATE POLICY of the same name is the idiomatic way to make a policy migration re-runnable (147 of the 206 drops in the tree). Refined to flag only a policy dropped and NOT re-created under the same name on the same table: 14 of 207. Re-creating under a DIFFERENT name still counts as removal, because a narrower replacement is still a narrowing - which is precisely the US-627 shape and precisely what Release N+1 will do again. || ROUND 6 2026-08-19 (loop) - the REFRESH CYCLE, which is the whole reason useSignedProfilePicture exists rather than one createSignedUrl at render, had NO test coverage at all. Reading it found the defect the missing tests were hiding: on a failed re-mint the hook logged, fell back to the stored public URL, and STOPPED - no further attempt, ever. Invisible today (the bucket is public, the fallback works, the avatar looks fine) and a broken image at Release N+1, where a signed URL is the only read path: one transient failure on the 540s tick leaves that avatar broken until the page reloads, and the tick runs on every mounted avatar. FIXED: bounded backoff 5s/15s/45s/120s then stop, with a success resetting the counter so a long session does not exhaust its retries on unrelated blips hours apart. Bounded deliberately - surviving a blip is the goal, not hammering storage from every avatar on screen. SIX new tests where there were none: the 540s re-mint firing, the retry recovering, the backoff stopping at four, the timer clearing on unmount (a leak there would re-mint for every avatar the user ever scrolled past), and the delay table. Negative control run: removing the retry line fails exactly the two retry tests and nothing else. Full suite 1599 passed / 3 skipped. || ROUND 7 2026-08-19 (loop) - CORRECTION to a premise recorded in these notes twice. The Release N wiring deliberately excluded ManageKidsDialog:288 on the grounds that formData.profile_picture_url is 'a blob: preview of the file the user just picked, not a stored object'. That is true only AFTER a pick. Opening the dialog to EDIT an existing kid seeds formData from kid.profile_picture_url at line 158 - a stored object - and renders it, so the kid editor was the last render site for a stored photo still going through a bare AvatarImage. Invisible today (public bucket, plain URL loads) and a missing avatar at Release N+1, on the screen parents use to manage their children. Swapped to KidAvatarImage, which passes a blob: through untouched, so one component covers both cases and the distinction was never needed. OnboardingDialog's exclusion DOES hold - childData.profile_picture_url starts empty and is only ever assigned a URL uploaded in that session - and this time it was checked rather than assumed. Both pinned in src/lib/storageBucketPolicies.test.ts, including an assertion that fires if OnboardingDialog ever starts seeding from a kid record; verified the pin fails when the component is reverted. || ROUND 8 2026-08-20 (loop) - re-enumerated the render sites EXHAUSTIVELY instead of trusting the list in these notes, after last round's ManageKidsDialog miss. Found a SECOND missed site: ApplyTemplateDialog:233 renders a plain 24px inside a label rather than an Avatar, so it was invisible both to a search for AvatarImage and to the original enumeration - which had in fact NAMED the file among 'five files that read kid.profile_picture_url for rendering' and then never wired it. Added src/components/KidPhoto.tsx, the same idea as KidAvatarImage for the shape (a component rather than a hook call, because the site is inside a .map() over kids and a hook cannot be called per iteration; one instance per kid also gives each its own refresh timer; alt is required, since a child's photograph is content not decoration). THE PIN IS NOW A SWEEP, not a list: it walks every component and asserts exactly one - OnboardingDialog, whose value is only ever a fresh upload - renders a profile_picture_url through a bare img or AvatarImage. Enumerating by hand is precisely what let two sites through twice. Verified the sweep fails when ApplyTemplateDialog is reverted. Full suite 1602 passed / 3 skipped. || ROUND 9 2026-08-20 (loop) - US-628 (delete) and US-634 (sign) had each grown their OWN parser for turning a stored public URL back into (bucket, path). Merging them found THREE defects, each present in one and not the other. (1) parseStorageObjectUrl kept a #fragment, so storage.remove() was handed 'user-1/photo.jpg#top', which matches no object - the cleanup failed silently and left the replaced photo behind, against a Privacy Policy that promises deleting a child profile deletes the data. (2) parseStorageObjectUrl THREW a URIError on a malformed percent escape, and deleteStorageObject calls it BEFORE its try block while both call sites use `void deleteReplacedStorageObject(...)` - so one stray % in a stored URL was an unhandled rejection during the kid save flow rather than a logged failure. Reproduced both before fixing. (3) the signer accepted a path containing '..' (the delete path has refused that since US-628) and declined an already-signed URL; both now change for the better - traversal refused on the signing side too, and a signed URL re-signed rather than rendered as-is and never refreshed, which would have broken that avatar the moment its token expired. The signer delegates to US-628's parser now and adds only the bucket allowlist, which is the one thing it genuinely needs. Full suite 1606 passed. || CROSS-STORY FINDING 2026-08-22 (loop, from us-643-bucket-migrations-check.sql). With the three bucket migrations applied, an AUTHENTICATED role can list Assets (1 object) and blog-images (2) and sees ZERO in `images` - because 20260822000002 deliberately declares that bucket with no policies at all. That is correct for production (a permissive policy could only widen a bucket of photographs of children) and it has a consequence that is easy to miss: SELECT is exactly what createSignedUrl needs. In an environment built from these migrations alone, a kid photo in `images` CAN NEVER BE SIGNED. useSignedProfilePicture falls back to the stored public URL (src/hooks/useSignedProfilePicture.ts, verified), so nothing breaks while the bucket is public - and it breaks COMPLETELY at US-634's Release N+1, when public goes false and the signed URL is the only read path. SEQUENCING REQUIREMENT for US-634: the owner-scoped SELECT policy for `images` must land in the SAME migration that flips public = false, not in a follow-up. Measured, not reasoned: anon 0 / authenticated Assets 1, blog-images 2, images 0, on PostgreSQL 16.13. || ROUND 10 2026-08-22 (loop) - AC5 ('storage-object deletion from US-628 keeps working') TURNED OUT TO BE ALREADY BROKEN, before the bucket goes anywhere near private. THE ASYMMETRY: 20251008025307 wrote all four profile-pictures policies against the PATH, auth.uid()::text = (storage.foldername(name))[1]. 20260817000000 then scoped SELECT and deliberately added a second branch - OR owner = auth.uid() - because the path is only a proxy for ownership and misses objects uploaded before the convention settled. DELETE and UPDATE never got that branch. So for a legacy object the owning parent CAN READ their child's photo and CANNOT DELETE OR REPLACE IT. Measured on PostgreSQL 16.13, not reasoned: owner reads 2 objects, deletes 1, and the legacy one is still present afterwards. AND IT FAILS SILENTLY, which is why nobody noticed. storage.remove() on a row RLS forbids is NOT an error - it returns an empty list - and src/lib/storageCleanup.ts destructured only { error } and returned true unconditionally. Its own docstring promised 'false when the removal failed', and the Privacy Policy promise quoted in its own header (deleting a child profile deletes the data) was not being kept for these objects. THE TEST STUB WAS COMPLICIT: it returned { data: null } where a real remove() returns the array of objects it removed, so no assertion could tell 'removed one' from 'removed nothing'. Stub made faithful as part of this. FIXED BOTH HALVES. 20260822000003 gives DELETE and UPDATE the same owner branch SELECT has; verified against Postgres before and after - 2 read / 1 deleted / 1 left behind becomes 2 read / 2 deleted / 0 left behind. INSERT is deliberately untouched: a new object has no owner yet, and the folder check is what makes the path convention true. storageCleanup.ts now treats an empty result as 'nothing removed', logs it and returns false, so the next gap of this shape is loud. WHY THIS ONE COULD BE FIXED WHEN US-635's COULD NOT: these policy names come from a migration, so DROP POLICY can name them. The images bucket's policies were made in the dashboard and their names are unknown, which is the whole reason that one still waits. Both guards verified discriminating: reverting the client fix reds the RLS-denied test, dropping the owner branch reds the parity test. Migration applies and replays cleanly against PostgreSQL 16.13. VERIFIED: 1646 passed / 3 skipped, 9 gates, lint-ratchet at baseline 1234, ASCII clean. || ROUND 11 2026-08-22 (loop) - 'SO THE NEXT GAP OF THIS SHAPE IS LOUD' WAS NOT TRUE WHEN I WROTE IT. Round 10 made deleteStorageObject return false and log a warning on a removal that silently removed nothing, and called that loud. Checked it this round instead of repeating it: EVERY caller discards the boolean - ManageKidsDialog:206 and OnboardingDialog:151 both `void deleteReplacedStorageObject(...)`, KidsContext:171 awaits and ignores the result - and logger.warn reaches console.warn and NOTHING ELSE. src/lib/logger.ts has no Sentry path at any level. So an orphaned photograph of a child was being recorded in a browser console nobody reads, which is not meaningfully louder than the silence it replaced. FIXED PROPERLY: all three failure paths (RLS denied it, the API errored, the call threw) now go through one reportOrphanedObject helper that captures to Sentry with tag type=storage_orphan, behind the same MODE / VITE_SENTRY_ENABLED guard the rest of the codebase uses. Deliberately NOT routed through either existing logError - there are two, in sentry.tsx and api-errors.ts, and both stamp a `source` tag that is not this one; a compliance signal filed under the wrong source is a signal nobody finds. Three tests pin it, including that a successful removal reports nothing; reverting to the round-10 logger.warn reds two of them. AND I PUSHED A RED GATE IN ROUND 6, THE SAME ORDERING MISTAKE AS ROUND 2. check-migration-safety.sh flags 20260822000004 because it drops a policy and re-creates it under a DIFFERENT name, which the gate counts as a narrowing. It passed during round 6's validation only because the file was still UNTRACKED at that point, so the gate could not see it - exactly how the storage gate was fooled in round 2. Acknowledged with the escape hatch the gate documents, `-- migration-safety: allow drop-policy ()`, and with the check it actually asks for done rather than waved: no shipped client reads through that policy, because public-bucket reads bypass RLS, both callers hold the service-role key, and nothing anywhere calls list() on it. PROCESS FIX: gates now run AFTER `git add -A`, not before. Both times this bit, the difference was a file the gate could not see yet. || ROUND 12 2026-08-22 (loop) - RAN THE BUILD, WHICH IS A HARD CI GATE THIS SESSION HAD NEVER TOUCHED. ci.yml's Build job runs `npx vite build`, and 16 rounds of work had gone onto this branch verified by tests, gates and typecheck but never by the build itself. That matters most for round 11's change, which added a MODULE-SCOPE `import * as Sentry from '@sentry/react'` to src/lib/storageCleanup.ts - a lib pulled in by KidsContext, ManageKidsDialog and OnboardingDialog. A new heavyweight import in a widely-imported lib is exactly how a 381kB vendor chunk gets dragged somewhere it was not before. IT IS CLEAN. `npx vite build` exits 0 in 48s. Built origin/main the same way for comparison: 312 JS chunks on both sides, none added, none removed, and the total grows by 300 bytes - +298 of that in `index`, which is my code, plus a few bytes of minifier churn in three unrelated chunks. Sentry stays in exactly one vendor-sentry chunk and is referenced by two chunks in all, the same as before; the import is free because main.tsx already initialises Sentry in the same graph. MY OWN COMPARISON SCRIPT WAS WRONG AND I CAUGHT IT. The chunk-name normaliser used `-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}\.js$` to strip the content hash, but the hyphen inside that character class let it swallow `-sentry-CasAKxMS.js`, so the sentry-specific assertion was silently comparing a chunk called `vendor` and proved nothing. It reported an empty list for BOTH sides, which reads like a clean result. Redone with the hyphen removed from the class: one vendor-sentry chunk, confirmed. The size comparison was never affected - both sides used the same normaliser - but the assertion I was about to quote was vacuous.

userStories.title: Audit the undeclared images bucket that iOS uploads kid photos to
userStories.description: As a parent using the iOS app, I want the bucket my child's photo actually lands in to be as locked down as the web one, so that closing the web hole is not mistaken for closing the hole.
acceptanceCriteria: ios/EatPal/EatPal/Services/ImageUploadService.swift:8 uploads to a bucket named 'images', not profile-pictures. No migration in supabase/migrations creates it - it was made out-of-band in the Supabase dashboard, so its public flag and its RLS policies cannot be read from the repo
Check the dashboard: is storage.buckets.public true for 'images', and what SELECT policies exist on storage.objects for it

If an unrestricted SELECT policy exists, replace it the way US-627 did for profile-pictures. Scope on storage.objects.owner rather than the path: objects are stored at kids/{kidId}-{unixSeconds}.jpg (ImageUploadService.swift:40) with no user-id folder, so folder-based scoping is not possible
Declare the bucket in a migration with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING so its configuration stops living only in the dashboard
kids/{kidId}-{unixSeconds}.jpg is guessable given a kid id: change the iOS path to use UUID().uuidString, matching the US-627 web fix
Confirm no shipped iOS build calls list() on this bucket before tightening SELECT - ImageUploadService only calls upload/getPublicURL/remove, so verify nothing else does
Extend src/lib/storageBucketPolicies.test.ts to cover the images bucket once it is declared in a migration
userStories.notes: Found 2026-08-17 while implementing US-627. iOS is the live product, so this is where kid photos actually come from in production - which makes it at least as exposed as the web bucket US-627 closed, possibly more. Cannot be fully fixed from the repo: the bucket does not exist in any migration, so its current policy set is unknown and a migration written blind could either no-op (if the real policy has a different name than the one dropped) or fail to override an unknown permissive policy, since RLS policies are OR'd and a new one cannot restrict an existing one. Needs a dashboard check first, then a migration. Filed rather than folded into US-627 because it needs out-of-band information. || PROGRESS 2026-08-19 (loop) — did the two ACs that do not need the dashboard, and verified a third. GUESSABLE PATH FIXED: ImageUploadService.swift built kids/{kidId}-{unixSeconds}.jpg, which given a kid id is roughly 86400 guesses for a known day against a bucket that is public-read by URL for shipped builds. Now kids/{UUID().uuidString}.jpg, matching what US-627 did for the web (ManageKidsDialog/OnboardingDialog use ${user.id}/${generateId()}). Checked it was safe first: all three call sites pass an id and use only the RETURNED url, ImageUploadService.delete is never called from Swift, and nothing anywhere parses or reconstructs an image path, so dropping the id from the filename breaks nothing. The `id` parameter is kept in the signature — an unused Swift function parameter is not a warning, and removing it would have touched three call sites in code this container cannot compile. Deliberately did NOT also add a {userId}/ folder like the web has: it would enable path-based RLS scoping, but the bucket's INSERT policy is dashboard-only and an unknown policy could be asserting the current path shape. AC CONFIRMED: nothing calls list() on storage anywhere in the Swift app — the only storage operations in ios/ are upload, getPublicURL and remove — so tightening SELECT will not break a shipped build. PINNED: src/lib/storageBucketPolicies.test.ts now checks the Swift source text for UUID().uuidString and the absence of timeIntervalSince1970 (source text because there is no Swift toolchain in CI); verified it goes red on the old path and green on the new one. NOT COMPILED — no Xcode here, so the change is reviewed, not built. STILL BLOCKED ON THE DASHBOARD: whether storage.buckets.public is true for 'images', what SELECT policies exist, declaring the bucket in a migration, and extending the policy test to cover it. Those cannot be written blind — RLS policies are OR'd, so a new policy cannot restrict an existing permissive one, and a DROP POLICY naming the wrong policy would silently no-op. || 2026-08-19 (loop) — turned the dashboard step from a research task into a paste. supabase/diagnostics/us-635-images-bucket.sql is READ ONLY (three SELECTs, no DDL, and it lives OUTSIDE supabase/migrations so nothing applies it — confirmed check-migration-prefixes still passes and nothing in CI or the workflows references the directory). It answers the exact three things the follow-up migration needs: (1) is storage.buckets.public true for 'images' — which matters more than it sounds, because a public bucket serves objects through the storage API WITHOUT consulting RLS, so if it is true then tightening policies alone changes nothing for anyone holding a URL; (2) every policy on storage.objects whose qual or with_check mentions the bucket, WITH the roles column — {public} there includes anon, which is precisely what made profile-pictures enumerable before US-627; (3) how many existing objects have a NULL owner. That third query is the one worth having found: objects land at kids/{uuid}.jpg with no user-id folder, so scoping has to key on storage.objects.owner rather than storage.foldername(name)[1] the way profile-pictures does — and if any rows have a null owner, an owner-scoped SELECT policy would make them unreadable to EVERYONE, including the parent who uploaded them. That needs a backfill before the policy is tightened, and nobody would have noticed until photos started disappearing. The file also records what each combination of answers implies, so the decision is written down rather than re-derived. STILL BLOCKED: someone has to run it against production and paste the output back. || ROUND 2 2026-08-19 (loop) - this story is now a hard prerequisite for US-634, not an independent audit. US-634 plans to flip profile-pictures to public=false, which does nothing for a kid photo uploaded from iOS, because those live in THIS bucket (ImageUploadService.swift:8). Same column, two buckets. Added query 4 to supabase/diagnostics/us-635-images-bucket.sql: it splits public.kids by which bucket profile_picture_url points into (profile-pictures / images / inline / external / none). That count is what decides whether US-634 can close as scoped or has to cover both buckets, and it is one SELECT on a table this repo owns. Column name verified against src/integrations/supabase/types.ts (kids.profile_picture_url). Still BLOCKED on the same single user action: run the file against production and paste the output. || ROUND 3 2026-08-19 (loop) - RAN THE DIAGNOSTICS instead of only reading it, against a Postgres 16 stand-in built to match Supabase's storage schema (storage.buckets, storage.objects, storage.foldername(), public.kids). The file executes clean, but query 2 WAS WRONG. It filtered policies to those whose qual or with_check mentions 'images'. A policy that names no bucket - USING (owner IS NOT NULL), for instance - applies to every object in EVERY bucket, which makes it the most permissive shape there is and the one this audit most needs to see; the filter hid it. Reproduced on the stand-in: with both a bucket-scoped policy and a bucket-agnostic public SELECT policy present, the query returned only the narrower one and read as reassuring. Query 2 now lists EVERY policy on storage.objects with an applies_to flag (images / another bucket / ALL BUCKETS) and the interpretation section says to read that column first, since RLS policies are OR'd and a permissive bucket-agnostic policy decides the answer whatever the images-specific ones say. Query 1 also broadened from two named buckets to all of them - 'images' was itself created in the dashboard and found only by reading the Swift client, so the same question applies to whatever else is in there. Verified with objects at a folder and at the bucket root, an owner-less object, four buckets and both policy shapes: psql exit 0, every query returning the expected counts. An empty top_folder row in query 3 is an object at the bucket root, not an error - noted in the file header. STILL BLOCKED on the same single user action: run the file against production and paste the output. || ROUND 3/4 2026-08-19 (loop) - RAN US-627's POLICY instead of trusting it. PostgreSQL 16 with a stand-in for Supabase's storage and auth schemas, the migration 20260817000000 applied verbatim. IT WORKS AS DOCUMENTED: before, anon enumerates all 4 seeded objects; after, anon 0, user A sees 2 (own folder plus a legacy object matched through the owner column - so that OR branch earns its place), user B sees 1 and none of A's, admin sees all 4. This is the first actual verification of the control that closed anonymous enumeration of a bucket full of photographs of children. NEW FINDING, and it is a US-634 pre-condition: an object with NO owner AND no user-id folder is visible to ADMINS ALONE - not to the parent whose child it is a photograph of. Harmless today (the bucket is public and the app falls back to the stored public URL) and BREAKING at Release N+1, because createSignedUrl requires the SELECT this policy denies, so a signed URL cannot be minted for such an object at all. Added query 5 to supabase/diagnostics/us-635-images-bucket.sql: profile-pictures objects split by whether they can be signed - via owner, via a first path segment that parses as a uuid, or neither. unsignable > 0 means US-634 needs an OWNER BACKFILL BEFORE the bucket is closed, not after. Verified against both awkward shapes (no owner + no folder, and no owner + a folder that is not a uuid). The proof is checked in as supabase/diagnostics/us-627-policy-check.sql - self-contained, runs against a throwaway database, expected output in its header. || ROUND 5 2026-08-22 (loop) - SPLIT THE BLOCKED PART FROM THE PART THAT NEVER WAS. This story sat wholly blocked on the dashboard read, but only two of its seven ACs actually need it. DECLARED, AC4: supabase/migrations/20260822000002_declare_images_bucket.sql creates the bucket and NOTHING else. public = true is forced by shipped clients, not guessed - ImageUploadService.swift:57 calls getPublicURL and stores the result, nothing in the Swift app signs, so phones in the field render that URL directly and a disaster-recovery instance serving those same phones has to be public too. The identical argument 20260817000000 made for profile-pictures. ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING makes it a no-op against production. WHY NO POLICIES, AND WHY THAT IS THE WHOLE REMAINING BLOCK: a permissive policy added here could only WIDEN access to a bucket of photographs of children. CREATE POLICY has no ON CONFLICT and permissive RLS policies are OR'd, so it cannot tighten an unrestricted SELECT that may already exist. Tightening means DROP POLICY, which needs the policy's NAME, which lives in the dashboard. So creating the bucket is strictly safe and creating policies is strictly not, and the migration stops at the line between them. AC5 was ALREADY DONE and unrecorded: ImageUploadService.swift:47 builds "{folder}/{UUID}.jpg", not the guessable "{kidId}-{unixSeconds}" the AC describes. AC6 VERIFIED AND PINNED: ImageUploadService is the ONLY Swift file in the repo that calls Supabase Storage - the two other files matching 'storage' do so in comments - and it calls upload, getPublicURL and remove only, never list(). That matters because tightening SELECT breaks list() but not a public-URL read, so a lister in the field is the one thing that would turn the fix into an outage. AC7 DONE, which AC4 had been gating: src/lib/storageBucketPolicies.test.ts now covers images - declared with ON CONFLICT, declared with no CREATE POLICY, absent from INTENTIONALLY_PUBLIC_BUCKETS - plus the two AC6 checks. All five new assertions verified discriminating: injecting a policy into the migration reds 2, adding a list() call reds 1, adding a second Swift storage caller reds 1. REMAINS, and it is now ONLY AC2 and AC3: run supabase/diagnostics/us-635-images-bucket.sql against production, and if an unrestricted SELECT policy exists, drop it by name and replace it owner-scoped. Everything that did not require production is done. || CROSS-STORY FINDING 2026-08-22 (loop, from us-643-bucket-migrations-check.sql). With the three bucket migrations applied, an AUTHENTICATED role can list Assets (1 object) and blog-images (2) and sees ZERO in `images` - because 20260822000002 deliberately declares that bucket with no policies at all. That is correct for production (a permissive policy could only widen a bucket of photographs of children) and it has a consequence that is easy to miss: SELECT is exactly what createSignedUrl needs. In an environment built from these migrations alone, a kid photo in `images` CAN NEVER BE SIGNED. useSignedProfilePicture falls back to the stored public URL (src/hooks/useSignedProfilePicture.ts, verified), so nothing breaks while the bucket is public - and it breaks COMPLETELY at US-634's Release N+1, when public goes false and the signed URL is the only read path. SEQUENCING REQUIREMENT for US-634: the owner-scoped SELECT policy for `images` must land in the SAME migration that flips public = false, not in a follow-up. Measured, not reasoned: anon 0 / authenticated Assets 1, blog-images 2, images 0, on PostgreSQL 16.13. || ROUND 6 2026-08-22 (loop) - RAN THE PRODUCTION DIAGNOSTIC AGAINST A STAND-IN, BECAUSE IT IS THE ONE FILE STILL BLOCKING THREE STORIES AND ITS OUTPUT DECIDES A MIGRATION ON A BUCKET OF PHOTOGRAPHS OF CHILDREN. THE DIAGNOSTIC IS SOUND. All five queries run clean (psql exit 0, zero errors) and each answers what its header claims: query 1 lists every bucket with images and profile-pictures first; query 2 flags the bucket-agnostic policy as ALL BUCKETS and sorts it FIRST, which is the whole point since a permissive bucket-agnostic policy decides the answer whatever the images-specific ones say; query 3 shows the kids folder and a blank top_folder row; query 4 splits kid photos by source bucket; query 5 reports 5 objects, 2 signable via owner, 1 via a uuid folder, 2 unsignable. TWO DEFECTS FOUND, BOTH IN THE VERIFICATION RATHER THAN THE QUERIES. (1) The header said 'all four queries run clean'. There are FIVE - query 5, the US-634 signability pre-condition, was added in a later round and had NEVER BEEN RUN. It works, but nobody knew that. (2) My first stand-in approximated storage.foldername with a regexp that strips the filename. Supabase's real function splits on '/' and drops the last element, and the two disagree EXACTLY at the bucket root: the regexp returns {'root.jpg'}, the real one returns an empty array. So query 3's documented 'an empty top_folder row is an object at the bucket root' was NOT reproducible under my harness - it printed the filename instead. With the real function it comes back blank, as documented. The guidance was right; my check of it was wrong. THE SAME APPROXIMATION WAS IN A FILE I WROTE IN ROUND 6 of US-643, us-643-bucket-migrations-check.sql. Corrected to the real implementation, copied from us-627-policy-check.sql, which had it right all along. Re-ran both: us-643 still 5 buckets / 11 policies / anon 0, us-627 still clean, so no earlier conclusion moves - the round-10 delete-parity finding used objects with and without a slash, where both implementations agree. HARNESS CHECKED IN as supabase/diagnostics/us-635-standin-check.sql with the expected output per query, so the header's claims are re-runnable instead of believed. STILL BLOCKED on the same single action, and it is now a better-understood one: run us-635-images-bucket.sql against production and paste the output. Read query 2's applies_to column first. || ROUND 12 2026-08-22 (loop) - THE PRODUCTION DIAGNOSTIC DID NOT ASK ITS OWN QUESTION ABOUT THE BUCKET IT IS NAMED AFTER. Query 5 counts objects that would become unreadable once signed URLs are the only read path - and its WHERE clause is `bucket_id = 'profile-pictures'`, full stop. There was no equivalent for `images`, the bucket the LIVE iOS app writes every kid, food and recipe photo into and the one this file exists to audit. Query 5 answered 'can profile-pictures be closed'; nothing answered 'can images be closed'. IT MATTERS MORE FOR images, NOT LESS. profile-pictures has two routes to signability - the owner column, or a first path segment that is the owner's uuid. images has ONE. ImageUploadService.swift:47 writes "{foods|recipes|kids}/{uuid}.jpg", so the first segment is a folder TYPE and never a user id, which is precisely why AC3 of this story says to scope on storage.objects.owner rather than the path. If owner is NULL on an images object, nothing can sign it, and at US-634's Release N+1 that photo is simply gone. ADDED query 6 (images: objects / signable_via_owner / unsignable / distinct_top_folders) and query 7 (every bucket, objects and owner-null counts, worst first) - the second so the NEXT dashboard-created bucket is not discovered the way this one was, by reading a Swift file. Both verified against the checked-in stand-in: images reports 2 objects, 1 signable, 1 unsignable; query 7 reports profile-pictures 5/3 and images 2/1. All seven queries run clean, psql exit 0, zero errors. The harness's expected-output header was updated IN THE SAME CHANGE, because round 9 of US-643 found exactly this file's header drifting after queries were added and nothing re-checked it. THIS SHARPENS THE SEQUENCING NOTE recorded earlier rather than replacing it: an owner-scoped SELECT for images must land in the same migration that flips public=false, AND a backfill has to precede both if query 6 returns unsignable > 0. A permissive policy added after the flip cannot help an object nobody could read in between. || ROUND 15 2026-08-22 (loop) - VERIFIED THE REPO-SIDE ACs RATHER THAN RE-READING THEM. The guessable-filename AC is DONE: ImageUploadService.swift:47 builds "\(folder.rawValue)/\(UUID().uuidString).jpg" and the kid id no longer appears in the path. The 'confirm nothing calls list()' AC is DONE and now checked rather than argued: grep across ios/**/*.swift finds no .list( at all. Also confirmed the random-name change broke nothing downstream - nothing anywhere in ios/ reconstructs a storage path from an id, so no caller depended on the old shape. THE CHECK TURNED UP SOMETHING ELSE: delete(path:) has zero call sites. Not 'no longer usable with random names' - never called. iOS has never deleted a storage object, on photo replace or on kid deletion, while the web does both (US-628). Raised as US-644 with the call sites; not fixed here because it is Swift and there is no toolchain in this container. ADDED QUERY 8 to us-635-images-bucket.sql to size it: objects in `images` that no kids or recipes row references, grouped by top folder. Verified end to end against the stand-in - harness and diagnostic both psql exit 0, zero errors, and all eight queries return exactly the counts the harness header now predicts (kids 3 objects / 2 unreferenced, recipes 2 / 1, bucket root 1 / 1). The harness gained a public.recipes table and four objects covering a superseded photo, a pre-US-635 guessable name, and a referenced-vs-orphaned recipe image. STILL BLOCKED, unchanged: the production read.

userStories.title: Grocery virtualized rows overlap: estimateSize underestimates real row height
userStories.description: As a user with more than 50 grocery items, I want the rows to stop overlapping each other so that I can read and tap the right item.
acceptanceCriteria: src/pages/Grocery.tsx:595-599 estimates 56px for an item row, but the row is `flex items-center gap-3 px-4 py-3` (24px vertical padding) and its tallest child exceeds 32px in two shipped cases, so rows are positioned closer together than they render
Case 1 (touch, any row): src/index.css:215-226 forces min-height 44px on every button under @media (pointer: coarse), so the qty/edit/delete controls make the row 44+24 = 68px against a 56px estimate
Case 2 (any pointer, rows with a photo): the thumbnail is w-10 h-10 (40px), so the row is 40+24 = 64px against the same 56px estimate
Only header rows get an explicit height (Grocery.tsx:826); item rows are positioned by transform: translateY(virtualRow.start) and size themselves, so each underestimate compounds down the list

Fix by measuring instead of estimating: pass ref={groceryVirtualizer.measureElement} and data-index on the row elements (@tanstack/react-virtual 3.13 supports dynamic measurement), rather than hand-tuning the constant, which cannot cover pointer type, photos and text wrapping at once
Verify in a browser at a coarse-pointer emulation with >50 items and at least one item having a photo_url; a source-only check cannot catch this
Confirm the same estimate pattern is not repeated on other virtualized lists in the codebase
userStories.notes: Found 2026-08-19 while finishing US-576. NOT caused by that change, which only flips opacity and is layout-neutral: the 44px controls were already occupying the row on touch, just invisible. Derived from reading the CSS and the JSX rather than measured in a browser, so the exact overlap in pixels should be confirmed before fixing; the mechanism (estimate 56 vs content 64-68) is solid, and the photo case makes it reproducible on desktop too. Only bites lists over 50 items, which is the useVirtualGrocery threshold at Grocery.tsx:590. || FIXED 2026-08-19 (loop), and the overlap is now MEASURED rather than reasoned about. Built a throwaway Chromium harness (Vite + the compiled Tailwind + the real row classNames, estimateSize and absolute/translateY positioning) rendering 60 rows, half with a w-10 photo, once with the shipped estimate-only setup and once with measureElement, and read getBoundingClientRect from both. RESULTS - fine pointer: rows are 53px bare and 65px with a photo against the 56px estimate, giving 11 overlapping row pairs, worst -9px. Coarse pointer: EVERY row is 69px, because the 44px button minimum from src/index.css:215 dominates and collapses the photo/no-photo difference, giving 22 overlapping pairs out of 22 - the entire list - worst -13px. So the touch case was worse than the story predicted: not some rows overlapping, all of them. With measureElement: 0 overlaps in both contexts. The earlier prediction of 64-68px was close but wrong in detail, and the code comment now carries the measured numbers instead. FIX: data-index + ref={virtualizer.measureElement} on the virtual rows, and the fixed height dropped from the group-header rows so they measure too. estimateSize is kept as a first-paint guess and documented as such. SAME PATTERN FOUND AND FIXED ELSEWHERE (the last AC): src/pages/Pantry.tsx:237 (estimateSize 64, wrapping PantryListItem) and src/pages/Recipes.tsx:155 (estimateSize 72, wrapping RecipeListItem) had the identical shape - absolutely positioned rows, fixed estimate, no measurement - and both wrap components carrying buttons, so they hit the same 44px-on-touch growth. Both got the same treatment. HONESTY NOTE: only Grocery's geometry was measured; Pantry and Recipes received the same mechanical change on the same reasoning, and measureElement is strictly more correct than a fixed estimate whatever the real row height turns out to be, so it cannot regress them. VERIFIED: full suite 1486 passed / 3 skipped, npm run build exit 0 with 14/14 routes, eslint findings on all three files byte-identical to the pre-change baseline (Grocery 5 pre-existing, Pantry 0, Recipes 0).

userStories.title: ensure-chromium.mjs fails the build when a usable Chromium is already installed
userStories.description: As a release engineer, I want the prerender browser check to use a Chromium that is already on the machine so that a blocked or failing download does not take down the deploy the script exists to protect.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/ensure-chromium.mjs resolves the browser only via playwright's chromium.executablePath(), then shells out to `npx playwright install chromium` and exits 1 if that fails (scripts/ensure-chromium.mjs:44-53)

That exit 1 fails `npm run build`, because build is `node scripts/ensure-chromium.mjs && vite build && node scripts/prerender.mjs` - vite never runs, so the failure mode is worse than the one the script was written to prevent

Reproduced 2026-08-19 in a sandboxed environment: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers holds a working chromium-1194, but the installed playwright wants build 1200, so executablePath() returns a path that does not exist and the script tries to download. The download was blocked (403 from the egress proxy) and the whole build died

Before falling back to a download, probe for an already-present browser: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH entries and the chromium symlink inside them, and any chromium-* build directory, not only the exact build the installed playwright pins
When such a browser is found, export/emit it as PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE, which scripts/prerender.mjs:257 already honours - the escape hatch exists, nothing populates it automatically
Confirm a mismatched build still prerenders correctly: chromium-1194 driving a playwright that pins 1200 produced 14/14 routes with correct meta, so an exact version match is not required
Consider whether a failed prerender should fail the deploy at all, given the script's own header says a failed prerender is how tryeatpal.com went unpublished
userStories.notes: Found 2026-08-19 while verifying US-574's AC4, which needed the prerendered output. Worked around locally with PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE=/opt/pw-browsers/chromium; the build then succeeded and prerendered all 14 routes, which is also the evidence that the version mismatch is harmless. Not folded into US-574 - unrelated to homepage meta, and it is a build/deploy concern. Whether this bites Cloudflare Pages depends on whether that builder can reach playwright.download.prss.microsoft.com; the script's premise is that it installs the package but not the binaries, so the download path is load-bearing there and the probe would just be a cheap extra safety net. It matters most for CI or sandboxed builders with egress rules. || FIXED 2026-08-19 (loop). NEW scripts/resolve-chromium.mjs holds one resolver used by BOTH scripts, which matters because they are separate node processes chained by && - an env var set in ensure-chromium cannot reach prerender, so the resolution has to be repeated rather than passed along, and doing it in one place is what guarantees the browser ensure-chromium accepted is the browser prerender launches. Order: explicit PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE, then playwright's own pinned build, then a disk probe over PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH and $HOME/.cache/ms-playwright for a plain `chromium` entry or any chromium-*/chromium_headless_shell-* build, newest build number first. It returns {executablePath, source} and prerender only passes executablePath when source is not 'pinned', so normal builds where playwright is happy are untouched. END-TO-END PROOF: with PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE UNSET - the exact condition that failed - `npm run build` now logs '[ensure-chromium] found an existing build on disk: /opt/pw-browsers/chromium' then '[prerender] using chromium (probed)' and exits 0 with 14/14 routes. Previously it died before vite ran. FAILURE PATH ALSO CHECKED: with PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH and HOME pointed at empty directories the script still exits 1, now with a message naming both escape hatches (set PLAYWRIGHT_CHROMIUM_EXECUTABLE, or PRERENDER=0). NEW TEST src/lib/resolveChromium.test.ts (11 tests) covers the probe against real temp directories: mismatched build numbers, headless-shell builds, newest-build preference (including a case where lexical and numeric order differ), the plain-`chromium` preference, symlink following, a directory that only looks like a build, the HOME fallback, and override precedence. It tests findExistingChromium rather than resolveChromium for the disk cases, because whether playwright's pinned build exists varies by machine and would make the tests flaky. LAST AC ANSWERED, deliberately NOT changed: a failed prerender should still fail the deploy. Shipping an un-prerendered site silently is the exact SEO regression US-570 exists to fix, so a blank-shell deploy is worse than a blocked one; PRERENDER=0 is the explicit opt-out for anyone who wants it. What changed is that the build no longer fails for a browser it already had. VERIFIED: full suite 1497 passed / 3 skipped, build exit 0 with no env override, eslint clean, ASCII clean.

userStories.title: Sweep the app for JSX components used but never imported
userStories.description: As a user, I want components that render to actually render, rather than throwing ReferenceError on a code path nobody typechecked.
acceptanceCriteria: THREE INSTANCES FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-19: ManageKidsDialog.tsx used <AlertDialogTrigger> (line 505) with only the other eight AlertDialog members imported; AITicketAnalysis.tsx used <MessageSquare> and <RefreshCw>; CRMIntegration.tsx used <Plus>

The ManageKidsDialog one is a live user-facing crash, not an admin corner: the trigger sits inside {editingId && ...}, so clicking Edit on a child throws ReferenceError and takes the dialog down. It landed 2026-06-27 in merge 05ddb48 and sat for nearly two months

Root cause is the same one US-553 hit with SeoAnalysisTabs and <Input>: ESLint's no-undef is off for TS because TypeScript is supposed to cover it, and the full `tsc -b` is a NON-BLOCKING ratchet (ci.yml:66) that only fails when the error COUNT grows - so a genuine TS2304 can hide inside a backlog of 1257

A repo-wide tsc sweep is not viable in an agent container: scoping tsc to src/lib alone, or src/hooks alone, times out at 4 minutes because the import graph drags in AppContext and the generated supabase types. That is why scripts/ci/check-seo-extraction.sh is scoped to one directory

Follow-up: make the detector permanent. Either extend the scoped-typecheck gate directory by directory as trees are cleaned up, or add a lint rule / cheap AST check that compares JSX element names against imported and locally-declared bindings

The heuristic used here has known false positives worth encoding: destructured components ({ icon: Icon }), renamed props (as: Tag = 'div'), runtime destructuring (const { View, Text } = RNComponents), and generic type arguments (<K>, <HTMLInputElement>)
userStories.notes: Found 2026-08-19 by generalising the US-553 <Input> bug rather than treating it as a one-off. Scanned every non-ui .tsx in src/ for JSX element names, parsed each file's real import bindings (honouring default imports, multi-line named blocks and `as` aliases) and its local declarations, and diffed. First pass with a crude 'is the name mentioned anywhere' check gave 60 candidates, almost all noise; proper import parsing cut it to 18, of which 3 were real and 14 are the false-positive classes listed above. All three are fixed in this commit. THE DETECTOR IS NOT WIRED IN - it was a one-off script, so this story stays open until the check is permanent. Verified after the fixes: full suite 1556 passed / 3 skipped, build exit 0 with 14/14 routes, and eslint error counts on all three files identical to HEAD (5 on ManageKidsDialog, all pre-existing unused-var findings), so adding the imports introduced nothing new. || DETECTOR MADE PERMANENT 2026-08-19 (loop). scripts/ci/check-jsx-imports.mjs is now a HARD gate in ci.yml, next to check-committed-secrets and check-function-trees, plus `npm run check:jsx-imports`. It compares every JSX element name against the names each file actually BINDS — imports (default, named, aliased, namespace), declarations, and destructuring patterns — across all 383 non-ui components in under a second. Hard from day one because there is nothing pre-existing to burn down: it is clean on the current tree. GETTING TO ZERO FALSE POSITIVES TOOK TWO REAL FIXES, both worth recording. (1) The first version stripped string and template literals before scanning, and the single-quote pattern RAN AWAY on an apostrophe in ordinary prose ("doesn't"), pairing it with a later quote and swallowing everything between — 14k characters of Pantry.tsx, including the `function LoadingSkeleton` declaration it then reported as missing. It now strips comments only, line by line, so a runaway cannot cross a newline. That bug was found by distrusting the detector's own output rather than filing its six findings as issues. (2) Generic type parameter lists (`<K extends keyof T>`) parsed as elements; now skipped when `extends` follows. VALIDATED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: green across the whole tree, and confirmed to go red on each of the four bugs this class has actually produced — removing the Input import from SeoAnalysisTabs, AlertDialogTrigger from ManageKidsDialog, Plus from CRMIntegration and MessageSquare from AITicketAnalysis each fails the gate naming the file and the component. FALSE-POSITIVE CLASSES HANDLED rather than allowlisted: destructured components ({ icon: Icon }), renamed props with defaults (as: Tag = 'div'), runtime destructuring (const { View, Text } = RNComponents), and generic type arguments. All 7 gates pass; full suite 1556 passed / 3 skipped.

userStories.title: Web and mobile pantry disagreed on what a negative quantity means
userStories.description: As a parent, I want the pantry to say the same thing about a food on my phone and on the web, rather than one calling it low stock and the other out of stock.
acceptanceCriteria: FIXED 2026-08-19. src/components/pantry/pantryConstants.ts getStockStatus used `if (qty === 0) return 'out'`, while src/lib/foodFilters.ts foodStock used `if (qty <= 0) return 'out'`. A negative quantity therefore rendered as 'low' on web and 'out' on mobile
These are two parallel implementations of one rule, not a shared helper: FoodCard.tsx and PantryListItem.tsx call getStockStatus, app/(tabs)/pantry.tsx line 337 calls foodStock

LATENT, NOT LIVE: both platforms clamp their own decrement at zero (PantryListItem guards `if (qty > 0)`, app/(tabs)/pantry.tsx uses Math.max(0, ...)), so the UI cannot produce a negative. It is reachable from the native iOS app, a bulk import, or a direct edit, and there is no CHECK constraint on the column
getStockStatus now uses `<= 0`, matching mobile, with a comment saying why the comparison is not `=== 0`
src/lib/foodFilters.test.ts pins the two implementations to identical answers across -5, -1, 0, 0.5, 1, 2, 2.5, 3, 99, undefined and null; verified the test goes red when the old `=== 0` is restored

Consider whether a CHECK (quantity >= 0) constraint is wanted, which would make the question moot - additive and backward-compatible per CLAUDE.md only if no existing row violates it, so it needs a count first
userStories.notes: Found 2026-08-19 by generalising a different bug class rather than by looking for this. Wrote a detector for symbols exported from more than one module, after the duplicate SeoImageAnalysisTab in US-553. It returned 52 hits, and most were legitimate barrel re-exports - too noisy to ship as a gate, so it was NOT made permanent. One hit was real signal: LOW_STOCK_THRESHOLD defined in two modules. The constant agreed (2 in both), but the functions around it did not. WORTH RECORDING FOR NEXT TIME: my first read was 'foodFilters.ts is dead code, nothing imports it' - wrong, because I had grepped only src/ and the importer is app/(tabs)/pantry.tsx in the Expo tree. The module is not dead, it is the mobile half of a two-platform pair, which is exactly why it drifted. Fixed, pinned, and the drift-detection idea deliberately not turned into a gate because the signal-to-noise did not justify one. Verified: full suite 1566 passed / 3 skipped, all 7 gates pass, eslint clean.

userStories.title: Guard the exposure ladder against TypeScript/Swift drift
userStories.description: As a parent, I want my child's ladder to progress the same way whichever device I log an exposure from.
acceptanceCriteria: NO DRIFT FOUND 2026-08-19 - this is a guard, not a fix. src/lib/exposureLadder.ts and ios/EatPal/EatPal/Ladder/ExposureLadderPolicy.swift were compared by hand and agree completely
Constants match: advanceThreshold 2, repeatDays 2, cooldownDays 4, tantrumCooldownDays 7, autoPauseRefusals 2

All four outcome branches match, including mastery on a success at the top rung, hold-the-rung on partial, step-down plus auto-pause on the second consecutive refusal, and backed_off with a 7-day rest on tantrum

Both clamp at the bottom rung rather than underflowing, and both anchor date arithmetic to UTC - TS via Date.UTC, Swift via TimeZone(secondsFromGMT: 0) - so next_due_on cannot differ by a day for a parent west of GMT
src/lib/exposureLadder.parity.test.ts pins the five constants and the eight rung wire values against the Swift source text, since there is no Swift toolchain in CI

Known limit: source-text comparison cannot prove behavioural equivalence. It pins the numbers and the vocabulary, which is where a one-sided edit does its damage; the branch logic was verified by hand once and would need re-checking if either side is restructured
userStories.notes: Written 2026-08-19 after US-639, which found the pantry's stock-status rule quietly diverging between its web and mobile implementations on negative quantities. The ladder is the same shape of risk but a much worse blast radius: it decides which food a child is offered next and how fast they climb, so a one-sided edit means a child progresses differently depending on which device the parent used. Checked it expecting to find something and found nothing - the two implementations genuinely agree, including the easy-to-get-wrong parts (bottom-rung clamping, and UTC-anchored date math on both sides rather than a local-timezone formatter). Reporting the negative result rather than manufacturing a finding, and leaving behind the guard that was missing. VERIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: changing the Swift advanceThreshold to 3 fails the constant test, and renaming the tiny_taste rung's rawValue fails the rung test; restoring either goes green. The rung test compares the WIRE values (Swift's rawValue, e.g. `case tinyTaste = "tiny_taste"`) because that is what reaches food_attempts.stage, not the Swift identifier. Full suite 1574 passed / 3 skipped, all 7 gates pass.

userStories.title: Enforce the migration backward-compatibility rules in CI
userStories.description: As a release owner, I want a migration that would break shipped iOS builds to fail CI, rather than relying on everyone remembering a document.
acceptanceCriteria: IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-19. scripts/ci/check-migration-safety.sh flags DROP COLUMN, DROP TABLE, RENAME, SET NOT NULL, DROP POLICY and in-place ALTER COLUMN TYPE in migrations ADDED on the branch

Diff-scoped against the base ref, like no-new-any.sh, so the existing tree is untouched. That matters: 20260513000000_drop_user_profiles_scaffold.sql legitimately drops eleven leftover template tables (projects, teams, materials, financial_*) and carries its own refuse-if-data-present guard, and a whole-tree gate would fail on it forever and get switched off

Escape hatch with a REQUIRED reason: `-- migration-safety: allow drop-column (US-123, release N+1 of a completed deprecation)`. The point is not to forbid these forever - the CLAUDE.md flow ends with retiring the old shape - but to make it a deliberate reviewable line rather than something noticed after it ships
Comment lines are excluded from matching, so a migration that merely mentions DROP COLUMN in its header (as 20260817000000_scope_profile_picture_reads.sql does) is not flagged
Skips with a notice when the base ref is unavailable, so a shallow clone degrades rather than failing
Wired into ci.yml and `npm run check:migration-safety`

Extended 2026-08-19: also fails when a migration CREATEs a table that never gets ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. Collected across the branch's new migrations rather than per file, since creating a table in one and enabling RLS in the next is legitimate
userStories.notes: Written 2026-08-19 after noticing that CLAUDE.md's Migration Rules section - the one that exists because the DB is shared with every shipped iOS build still on a phone - had NO enforcement anywhere. The rules were a document, and the consequence of breaking them is a migration you cannot roll back out of the App Store. Checked the current tree first: only two migrations match the patterns at all, and neither is a violation. 20260513000000 drops eleven tables, but they are leftovers from a different app template (projects, teams, materials, financial_records) and it refuses to run if they contain data; 20260817000000 only MENTIONS the forbidden statements in a comment, which is why the checker excludes comment lines. VERIFIED END TO END: committed a migration doing `ALTER TABLE public.kids DROP COLUMN nickname` and the gate failed naming the file, the line, why it breaks an old client, and the exact escape-hatch comment to add; removing the commit returned it to green. Also confirmed the escape hatch is recognised and that the three patterns (drop-column, set-not-null, rename) each fire independently. An earlier attempt to test it by STAGING the file rather than committing showed 'no new migrations' - the gate diffs commits, not the index - which was my test being wrong rather than the gate. Eight gates now pass; full suite 1574 passed / 3 skipped. || RLS CHECK ADDED 2026-08-19. CLAUDE.md also says 'Always enable RLS on new tables', and nothing enforced that either. Audited the whole tree first rather than assuming: 304 tables are created across all migrations and ALL 304 get ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, so there is no backlog and this can be hard from day one. The consequence of missing it is not subtle - a table without RLS is readable AND writable by anyone holding the anon key, which ships inside the client. Verified both directions with real commits: a migration creating public.widget_notes with no RLS fails naming the table and the fix, and adding ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY plus a policy to the same file turns it green. The check collects created-tables and RLS-enabled-tables ACROSS all migrations added on the branch, so the legitimate pattern of creating in one migration and enabling in the next is not flagged. Same `-- migration-safety: allow no-rls (<reason>)` escape hatch as the other rules.

userStories.title: Regenerate the Coolify combined migration bundles with correct encoding
userStories.description: As whoever runs the Coolify deployment, I want the combined migration SQL to be valid UTF-8 without a BOM so that psql does not fail on line 1 and the migration comments are not mojibake.
acceptanceCriteria: coolify-migration/combined_eatpal_migrations.sql and _clean.sql regenerated by create-combined-migration.ps1 on a Windows machine
Neither file starts with a UTF-8 BOM
The meal_voting vote_emoji comment reads as the intended emoji rather than Latin-1 mojibake
The SKIP entry for these two files is removed from scripts/ci/check-invisible-chars.mjs and the gate still passes
userStories.notes: Found 2026-08-19 by the new invisible-character gate. The generator had two encoding bugs, both FIXED IN THE SCRIPT here but not executable from this container (no PowerShell): Get-Content without -Encoding read each migration through the system ANSI codepage on Windows PowerShell 5.1, which is why the committed dumps show the meal_voting emoji comment as the Latin-1 rendering of its UTF-8 bytes; and Set-Content -Encoding UTF8 writes a BOM on 5.1, which makes psql report a syntax error on line 1. The script now reads with -Encoding UTF8 and writes via UTF8Encoding($false). The two committed dumps are ~20k lines of generated SQL and were deliberately NOT hand-edited - the right repair is to re-run the fixed generator. Until then they are excluded from the gate by an explicit SKIP with this reason attached. USER ACTION: run coolify-migration/create-combined-migration.ps1 on Windows, commit the regenerated files, drop the SKIP. || CLOSED 2026-08-19 (loop). packages.microsoft.com turned out to be reachable through the proxy, so PowerShell 7.6.5 was installed and the generators were RUN rather than reasoned about - which found a defect far larger than the encoding one. THE BUNDLE WAS NEVER VALID SQL. The wrapper is a plain DO $$ ... $$ per migration, and dollar quotes do not nest unless the tags differ; most migrations define a function or trigger and carry their own $$, so the first one closed the wrapper early and every line after it parsed as top-level SQL. On a clean Postgres 16: 1280 syntax errors, 3469 errors total, ending in an unterminated dollar-quoted string. It cannot ever have deployed. Wrapper now uses $eatpal_migration$ (unique against $$, $function$, $ep_md$, $pol$ and every other tag the migrations use) and the generator refuses to build if a migration ever contains that tag. AFTER: 0 syntax errors, 0 psql-level errors; the bundle's own summary reports 207 total / 21 applied on a bare Postgres, and 162 applied once an auth schema, uuid-ossp, pgcrypto and the anon/authenticated/service_role roles exist - the remaining 45 all name something else the stand-in lacks (storage, vector, realtime), i.e. environment, not bundle. ALSO FOUND: create-clean-migration.ps1 had BOTH encoding bugs its sibling had, which is why both dumps were mangled - only the sibling had been fixed. And both resolved ..\supabase\migrations against the CALLER's working directory with a Windows-only separator while the output path used $PSScriptRoot, so they only ran from inside that folder on Windows; now [IO.Path]::Combine on $PSScriptRoot. ACs: both bundles regenerated (no BOM, meal_voting emoji comment correct, 207 migrations), and the SKIP is removed from check-invisible-chars.mjs with the gate still passing. CAVEAT ON AC 1: regenerated with PowerShell 7.6.5 for LINUX, not on Windows. The output is byte-equivalent modulo the Generated: timestamp - the script builds its content with explicit `n and writes via WriteAllText, so no platform line-ending or BOM difference applies - and a Linux run allowed the SQL to actually be executed, which a Windows run here could not have. NEW GATE: scripts/ci/check-powershell-parses.sh parses every .ps1 (15 files, all parsing; verified it fails on an unclosed if). CLAUDE.md records two .ps1 files sitting unparseable for months, and nothing in this repo ever runs one, so the parser is the only thing that would have caught them. pwsh is preinstalled on GitHub's ubuntu runners.

userStories.title: Make the storage bucket inventory match reality
userStories.description: As whoever rebuilds an environment, I want every storage bucket the app uses to exist in a migration so that a fresh instance is not missing one silently.
acceptanceCriteria: The current public flag and RLS policies of the Assets bucket are read out of production (queries 1 and 2 of supabase/diagnostics/us-635-images-bucket.sql already cover every bucket)
A migration creates the Assets bucket with INSERT INTO storage.buckets ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, matching production's public flag
Its SELECT policy is declared alongside, or the reason it needs none is recorded

Each of blog-images, recipe-images, private-files and backups is either created by a migration or removed from STORAGE_BUCKETS in src/lib/storage-manager.ts, so the admin storage screen stops advertising buckets that do not exist
The storage_buckets_config seed in 20260110000000 is reconciled with whatever is decided above
Assets is removed from PENDING in scripts/ci/check-storage-buckets.mjs and the gate still passes with no registry-only note
userStories.notes: Found 2026-08-19 by scripts/ci/check-storage-buckets.mjs on its first run. src/lib/exitIntentGuide.ts:26 serves picky-eater-food-chaining-guide.pdf from a bucket named 'Assets' that no migration creates - the same class of problem as US-635's 'images', and the second instance the gate turned up. It fails QUIETLY: getPublicUrl only builds a URL string, it never checks that the bucket or object exists, so a missing bucket produces a lead-magnet email containing a link that 404s, with no error anywhere. Only TWO buckets are created by migrations at all (profile-pictures in 20251008025307, generated-images in 20260630000000); everything else in this project exists because someone clicked in the dashboard. SEPARATELY, and not blocking this story: public.storage_buckets_config seeds four buckets that no migration creates (blog-images, recipe-images, Assets, private-files), and the admin storage screen reads that table - so it lists buckets that may not exist. The generated_images migration's own comment already noticed this for two of them. The gate reports it as a note rather than a failure. BLOCKED on the same dashboard read as US-635; declaring the bucket blind risks writing a public flag that contradicts production. || WIDENED 2026-08-19 (loop). The gate was blind to the web app's own bucket registry: storage-manager.ts resolves buckets from a typed STORAGE_BUCKETS record and calls .from(config?.name || bucketName), so a literal-only scan sees a dynamic expression and finds nothing. Reading the record too takes the count from 2 declared / 4 referenced to 2 declared / 8 referenced. The four extra - blog-images, recipe-images, private-files, backups - have ZERO call sites anywhere outside the record itself, so nothing breaks today; but StorageManagement.tsx renders a tab per getAllBuckets() entry, so the admin screen presents six buckets of which exactly one is known to exist, and storageManager.upload() would silently target a non-existent bucket the day someone passes one of those names. 'backups' is not even in the storage_buckets_config seed, so there are three separate inventories disagreeing: migrations (2), the storage-manager record (6), and storage_buckets_config (5). The gate reports registry-only buckets as a note rather than a failure, since a name nobody calls cannot break a deploy. || ROUND 2 2026-08-22 (loop) - THE PREVIOUS ROUND'S CENTRAL CLAIM WAS WRONG, AND SO WAS THE GATE. It recorded that blog-images, recipe-images, private-files and backups 'have ZERO call sites anywhere outside the record itself, so nothing breaks today'. blog-images has two: functions/agent-blog-writer/index.ts:22,65,70 and functions/update-blog-image/index.ts:33,158,174 both upload a hero image to it and call getPublicUrl, storing that URL on the blog post. It is a live, load-bearing, undeclared bucket - the exact thing this story exists to catch - and it was filed as a harmless registry entry. WHY THE GATE MISSED IT: check-storage-buckets.mjs matched storage.from('literal') only, and both functions hoist the name into `const STORAGE_BUCKET = 'blog-images'` first. The same blind spot the gate already documented for storage-manager.ts, in a shape nobody had looked for. The gate now resolves single-assignment string constants before matching, which takes the count from 4 buckets with a call site to 5 and turns blog-images from a note into a hard failure. FAILURE MODE IT WAS HIDING: agent-blog-writer:69 catches the upload error and silently returns the provider URL, and getPublicUrl only builds a string - it never checks the bucket exists. So a rebuilt environment keeps publishing posts whose images point at a bucket that is not there, with no error anywhere. DECLARED: supabase/migrations/20260822000000_declare_blog_images_bucket.sql, public=true with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. The public flag is READ OFF THE CALL SITES rather than guessed, which is what unblocked this one where Assets and images stay blocked: the stored URL is a getPublicUrl result rendered in a public blog post, so anonymous read is the feature. ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING leaves production's own flag untouched; the migration only decides what a fresh environment gets. Policies mirror generated-images (public SELECT, authenticated write) and are preceded by DROP POLICY IF EXISTS so a replay is a no-op. blog-images added to INTENTIONALLY_PUBLIC_BUCKETS in storageBucketPolicies.test.ts. REGISTRY TRIMMED: recipe-images, private-files and backups genuinely do have zero call sites, so they are removed from STORAGE_BUCKETS rather than created - three real buckets to satisfy a registry nobody reads from is the wrong direction. The admin screen now renders 3 tabs instead of 6, two of which are declared. SECOND WRONG CLAIM, in the gate's own text: it said the admin storage screen reads storage_buckets_config. It does not - StorageManagement.tsx:98 calls storageManager.getAllBuckets(), the TS record. NOTHING in src, app, functions or ios queries that table at all. So the seed's phantom rows are dead data, not a screen listing buckets that do not exist, and the AC's 'reconcile the seed' is deliberately NOT done by a DELETE migration: writing one against a table with zero readers is migration risk for no benefit. The gate's note now says what is true. PINNED: src/lib/storageBucketScanner.test.ts, 7 tests running the real script in a throwaway git repo (the committedSecretsScanner pattern), because the regex was correct and its coverage was not - a unit test on the regex would have passed throughout. Verified the guard is discriminating: with the constant resolution removed, 3 of the 7 go red (inline still caught, constant and typed-constant missed, real-repo call-site count drops to 4); restored, 7 pass. One assertion was rewritten mid-round after it passed for the wrong reason - checking blog-images was absent from the registry note passes whether or not the gate can see the call site, since a declared bucket leaves that note either way. REMAINS: Assets is the last undeclared bucket with a real call site and is still blocked on the same production read as US-635 - unlike blog-images, nothing in the code fixes its public flag, since exitIntentGuide.ts only builds a URL and would look identical either way. || ROUND 3 2026-08-22 (loop) - LAST ROUND'S CLOSING LINE WAS WRONG, AND LAST ROUND'S COMMIT LEFT THE GATE RED. (1) It said Assets stays blocked because 'nothing in the code fixes its public flag, since exitIntentGuide.ts only builds a URL and would look identical either way'. It would not. exitIntentGuide.ts:25 puts that URL in an email queued to a lead, so the consumer is an inbox: no Supabase session, no anon key, and no signing code anywhere in the repo. A private bucket cannot serve that link at all, which fixes public = true as firmly as the blog case did. DECLARED in 20260822000001, ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, and removed from PENDING. The gate now reads 4 declared / 5 with a call site / 0 registry-only, exit 0, which is the 'no registry-only note' AC. (2) THE COMMIT THAT ADDED storageBucketScanner.test.ts LEFT THE GATE FAILING. The gate reads git ls-files and the gates were run BEFORE git add, so the green result was measured against a tree without the new file; once staged, the test's own fixtures ('probe-bucket', and 'literal' out of a doc comment) were scanned as real call sites. Fixed by skipping *.test.* and __tests__/ - a bucket referenced only by a test is not a production dependency - and pinned by a test that writes a fixture into a throwaway repo and asserts the gate stays green. (3) THE POLICY SHAPE IN 20260822000000 WAS COPIED FROM generated-images AND WAS WRONG. It created 'Public can view blog images' FOR SELECT with no TO clause, which applies to the public role including anon. userStories.title: iOS never deletes a replaced or removed kid photo
userStories.description: As a parent, I want deleting or replacing my child's photo to actually remove it from storage, so that a photograph of my child is not left at a public URL after I have removed it.
acceptanceCriteria: ImageUploadService.delete(path:) exists at ios/EatPal/EatPal/Services/ImageUploadService.swift and has ZERO call sites in the iOS app - confirmed by grep across ios/**/*.swift. Nothing on iOS has ever deleted a storage object

KidProfileEditorView.save() (ios/EatPal/EatPal/Views/Kids/KidProfileEditorView.swift:367) uploads a new photo and overwrites kids.profile_picture_url. The previous object stays in the bucket at the public URL it was handed out under
DataService.deleteKid (ios/EatPal/EatPal/Services/DataService.swift:120) deletes the row only, so removing a child leaves their photo in storage
The same applies to recipe images: RecipesView.swift:1647 and EditRecipeView.swift:294 upload through the same service and never delete

The web app already does this correctly and is the implementation to mirror: deleteReplacedStorageObject on replace (ManageKidsDialog, OnboardingDialog) and deleteStorageObject on delete (KidsContext.tsx:171), both parsing the URL back to (bucket, path) via parseStorageObjectUrl in src/lib/storagePaths.ts (US-628)

Swift needs the equivalent of parseStorageObjectUrl: split on /storage/v1/object/public/ (and /sign/), strip ?query and #fragment, take the first segment as the bucket and the rest as the path, and refuse a path containing '..'. src/lib/storagePaths.test.ts is the spec to mirror, including the malformed-escape case that threw an unhandled rejection on the web

Deletion must tolerate an RLS-blocked removal the way the web does: storage.remove() returns the list it actually removed, so an empty array is a silent no-op, not an error (see src/lib/storageCleanup.ts:56)

Whether existing orphans need a backfill is answered by query 8 of supabase/diagnostics/us-635-images-bucket.sql, which counts objects in `images` that no kids or recipes row references. That read is still blocked on US-635
This cannot be verified in the CI container: there is no Swift toolchain, and iOS is live in the App Store. Needs Xcode, like US-609
userStories.notes: Found 2026-08-22 (loop) while checking whether the US-635 random-filename change broke anything. It did not - delete(path:) has no callers, so nothing reconstructs a path - but that is the finding: nothing calls it at all. The web got object cleanup in US-628; iOS never did, and iOS is where the production kid photos come from (US-635's own framing). So 'delete my child's photo' does not delete it on the platform that took it. NOT A NEW EXPOSURE - the URL was already public while the photo was current - but it means removal is not removal, and the bucket only grows. Scope confirmed by grep rather than assumed: three upload call sites (KidProfileEditorView:367, RecipesView:1647, EditRecipeView:294), zero delete call sites, nothing calling .list(), and no code anywhere in ios/ reconstructing a storage path from an id. The web side is fine and tested - parseStorageObjectUrl is bucket-agnostic and src/lib/storagePaths.test.ts and storageCleanup.test.ts both cover the images-bucket URL shape - so a web user deleting a kid DOES clean up an iOS-uploaded photo, provided a DELETE policy on `images` allows it, which is a dashboard-only fact query 2 of the diagnostic will answer. NOT IMPLEMENTED HERE deliberately: the fix is a URL parser plus call sites in Swift, there is no Swift toolchain in this container, and iOS is live in the App Store. Writing code that cannot be compiled into a shipping app is the wrong trade.
